modules.name: Identity, sign-in & provisioning
modules.summary: We have email+password sign-in (two login pages), forgot/reset via email, change-password in Settings, and admin-created accounts with a shared team password plus forced first-login change. We lack OAuth/SSO, app-level lockout, IdP provisioning/SCIM, email aliases, multi-company membership and phone sign-in; access is one company per profile, set up by invite, pilot code or admin add-member.
modules.vsum: Strong: all OBSERVED claims matched the sign-in and provisioning articles; the two INFERRED articles now exist, with one (multi-instance) working differently from the artifact's guess.

features.name: Email and password sign-in
features.what: Gong-managed username and password, with password change and reset. Sessions end automatically after two weeks.
features.gn: Gong-managed username/password; 'automatically logged out after two weeks'.
features.on: Email+password sign-in on both login pages, forgot-password email, recovery page, and change-password panel in Settings. Session length is Supabase default, not a set 2-week policy.

features.name: Google, Microsoft and Salesforce sign-in
features.what: OAuth sign-in through Google, Microsoft or Salesforce. Salesforce sign-in needs a Salesforce admin to install Gong's external client app. Session length follows the provider's own policy (10 hours to 90 days).
features.gn: Google, Microsoft, Salesforce; logout 10 hours to 90 days per provider policy; Salesforce admin must install Gong's external client app.
features.on: No signInWithOAuth call anywhere in src; only password sign-in.

features.name: SAML SSO and OpenID Connect
features.what: Okta, Rippling and OneLogin via SAML, any other SAML provider, and OIDC. Default idle logout is 30 minutes; customisable for SAML.
features.gn: Okta, Rippling, OneLogin, other SAML, plus OpenID Connect; 30-min idle logout default, customizable for SAML only.
features.on: No SAML/OIDC or signInWithSSO usage found.

features.name: Mixed sign-in methods per company
features.what: An admin can enable any combination of sign-in methods at once; nothing forces one method.
features.gn: Admin can 'choose any combination' of methods.
features.on: Only one method exists, so there is nothing to mix; no per-company auth-method setting.

features.name: Account lockout after failed attempts
features.what: Five failed sign-in attempts lock the account for 60 minutes.
features.gn: Five failed attempts lock the account for 60 minutes; page doesn't say if it applies to SSO.
features.on: Sign-in calls Supabase straight from the browser; no app-level failed-attempt count or lockout. Only Supabase's built-in auth rate limits apply. Team API routes are rate limited, but not login.
ev: grep lockout|failed attempt src -> none for login

features.name: Provisioning from an identity provider
features.what: Team members sync from Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin, Rippling or Salesforce. Mandatory synced fields are first name, last name, job title and manager; the manager field builds the reporting hierarchy. Deactivating in the IdP deactivates in Gong.
features.gn: Okta, Salesforce, Rippling, OneLogin, Entra ID; mandatory first/last name, job title, manager; manager builds hierarchy; IdP deactivation deactivates.
features.on: No IdP sync or SCIM. People join by invite link, pilot code, or admin 'add agent' with a team password. Removal is a soft profiles.status='removed'.

features.name: Group-based assignments
features.what: Each IdP group maps to an assignment that sets seats, a permission profile per workspace, credit profile, data-capture settings and consent profile. Two update modes: automatic (Gong mirrors the IdP; admins cannot edit those fields in Gong) and manual (only name and manager keep syncing; everything else is set once and can drift).
features.gn: Assignments set seats, permission profile per workspace, credit profile, data capture, consent profile; automatic vs manual (manual syncs only first/last name and manager).
features.on: No IdP groups. The closest thing is setting role and access at invite time (InviteMemberDialog) plus the pilot-code module lock. Nothing keeps those settings synced afterward.

features.name: Multiple email addresses per person
features.what: A team member has a primary and additional email addresses so calls and emails from aliases match the same person. Basis: help article titled 'About primary and additional email address' exists in the index; content not read.
features.gn: Article exists: one primary plus additional company-owned alias emails, 'for identification only'; warns never to add personal emails.
features.on: One email per auth user; no alias table. Searched additional_email/email_aliases/user_emails.

features.name: Sign in to several company instances
features.what: One person can belong to more than one Gong company instance and switch between them. Basis: article 'Enable log in to multiple Gong instances' in the index; content not read.
features.gn: Article exists, but it isn't a membership model. Switching works via 'trusted authentication': the RA enables it, an admin adds a trusted account email, and a toggle allows switching without re-auth.
features.on: profiles.company_id is single-valued. The sidebar explicitly notes 'Multi-company switching isn't built'.

features.name: Phone-first sign-in for field reps
features.what: Gong has no phone-number or one-time-code sign-in; every method assumes a work email. Door-to-door reps often have only a personal phone. Proposal: SMS one-time-code sign-in as a peer route to email.
features.source: Absence inferred from https://help.gong.io/docs/set-sign-in-method (no phone method listed)
features.gn: Sign-in page lists no phone/SMS method and doesn't mention MFA. A web search found no Gong phone-OTP sign-in, so the absence still holds.
features.on: No signInWithOtp/phone sign-in. Reps still need an email; admin add-member gives a team password as a workaround.

modules.name: Company structure: workspaces, teams, seats
modules.summary: We have one company per account, with a flat org-tier role ladder (CEO..Supervisor..Member) and optional departments, but no manager-of-manager reporting tree. There are no workspaces, seats, Collaborator tier, self-serve purchase, bulk CSV team update or sandbox. Licensing is a per-company pilot-code module lock (care / sales_coach / complete), not per-person seats.
modules.vsum: Claims held up well; small slips on the 'mentioned/feedback' visibility wording and on how sandboxes are obtained today.

features.name: Workspaces
features.what: A workspace divides the instance by business line, region or use case. Calls live in the call owner's home workspace; emails live in every participant's workspace. Per-workspace: permission profiles, trackers, topics, call categories, scorecards, custom vocabulary, retention and automation rules. Shared: integrations, SSO, team members, accounts, privacy (except retention), API access.
features.gn: Calls in owner's home workspace; emails in every participant's workspace. Per-workspace and shared settings lists match the article.
features.on: No workspace concept; all data is scoped by company_id only.

features.name: Everyone can open every workspace
features.what: Users are not assigned to one workspace. Without a permission profile in a workspace they see only its homepage and calls shared with them, where they were mentioned, or where feedback was requested.
features.gn: 'Every team member can navigate to every workspace'. One sentence adds mentioned/feedback-requested calls, but the FAQ says only homepage + shared calls.
features.on: No workspaces. The nearest analogue is the module lock, which redirects a single-module account away from other modules rather than showing an empty state.

features.name: Move calls between workspaces
features.what: Users can move calls to another workspace; emails and texts cannot be moved in product. Moving a person does not move their history.
features.gn: Calls can be moved by users; email/text can't be moved in product (support only); moving a person doesn't move their history.
features.on: No workspaces, so nothing to move between.

features.name: Team hierarchy from manager field
features.what: Each person has a manager; the reporting tree drives 'my direct and indirect reports' scopes everywhere (calls, deals, coaching stats, forecast).
features.gn: Provisioning article: manager field 'is used to build the company hierarchy'. Permission page has direct/indirect-report scopes.
features.on: Org tiers (role ranks) and departments exist, but there is no manager_id. Sales Coach 'managers' (admins or sales_coach_role=admin) see the whole company, not just their reports.

features.name: Core seat plus application seats
features.what: Current model: Gong Foundation is the required core license; Enable Essentials, Forecast Essentials, Gong Forecast, Gong Engage and Data Cloud are application seats on top. Seats are toggled per person or in bulk; admin panel shows used vs available.
features.gn: Foundation core + Enable Essentials, Forecast Essentials, Gong Forecast, Gong Engage, Data Cloud. Seats are toggled per person or in bulk, with an in-use vs contract panel.
features.on: Entitlement is per company via a redeemed pilot code (care|sales_coach|elostate), not per-person seats. Per person there is only sales_coach_role/is_support_agent flags. crm_subscriptions.seat_count is an unbilled placeholder.

features.name: Free Collaborator users
features.what: A team member with no seat is a Collaborator: free, limited access (can receive shares, comments, feedback requests).
features.gn: No seat = Collaborator: limited access, costs nothing. Exact capabilities aren't listed.
features.on: An invited Member with no sales_coach_role is held on an in-module 'no access yet' screen. It's a waiting state, not a free tier with share/comment rights.

features.name: Self-serve seat purchase, prorated
features.what: Eligible companies buy more seats from the admin panel; usable immediately, prorated to term end, invoice in 2–3 days.
features.gn: 'Get more seats' for eligible companies; usable immediately, prorated to term end, invoice within 2-3 days.
features.on: Billing is stubbed; Stripe fields are reserved but unused.

features.name: Bulk team changes by CSV
features.what: Admins update many team members at once from a CSV file. Basis: article 'Make bulk changes via a CSV file' in index; columns not read.
features.gn: Article exists. CSV updates existing users only (can't add/remove users or change data capture). Columns include email, manager email, title, aliases. Validates, previews, applies in background.
features.on: No CSV/bulk team import or update. Members are added one at a time. CSV parsing exists only for schedule upload.

features.name: Sandbox instance
features.what: Enterprise plans include sandboxes for testing configuration. Basis: legacy Enterprise plan lists sandboxes; FAQ article exists.
features.gn: Legacy Enterprise lists sandboxes, but the FAQ says a Sandbox is a free, empty, separate instance any customer requests via their RA, with emails unique across instances.
features.on: No sandbox flag on companies. The /dashboard/smoke-test and /demo routes are test surfaces, not isolated tenants.

modules.name: Permission profiles & data access
modules.summary: Our access model is fixed roles: company admin (CEO/CFO/COO/admin), Sales Coach admin vs staff, support-agent flag, and a per-company module lock, all enforced in RLS. Reps see their own pitches and managers see the whole company. We lack named, configurable permission profiles, per-domain team scopes, per-page toggles and seat gating. Per-recording sharing exists only as a rep-consented 'team example' log.
modules.vsum: Nearly all claims confirmed on the permissions page (flagged stale, last updated 2026-10-12); one list mixed dashboards/metrics/targets into Business admin.

features.name: Named permission profiles
features.what: Admins define profiles and assign one per user per workspace.
features.gn: Profiles per workspace. llms.txt lists API list-all (/v2/all-permission-profiles), list users (/v2/permission-profile/users), plus retrieve/create/update (paths not shown).
features.on: No named profiles. Fixed role sets in code (ADMIN_ROLES, sales_coach_role admin|staff) are mirrored in SQL by admin_roles() and is_sales_coach_manager().

features.name: Call access scopes
features.what: Calls on/off; then all calls, or: calls they participated in, calls their direct and indirect reports participated in; advanced: calls of anyone on their manager's team, calls from specific teams; plus account-based access.
features.gn: All calls; participated; direct+indirect reports; advanced manager's team / specific teams; separate account-based toggle; shared calls are always visible.
features.on: RLS on pitch_scores: own pitches, or every pitch in the company if a manager. There are no report-tree, specific-team or account scopes.

features.name: Email access scopes
features.what: Same scope ladder as calls, applied to captured emails.
features.gn: Email scope mirrors calls: all / sent-received / reports / manager's team / specific teams + account toggle.
features.on: We don't capture rep emails, so there's no email scope.
ev: grep 'create table.*email' migrations -> no captured-email table

features.name: Deals, coaching, insights and forecast scopes
features.what: Each has the ladder: all / manager's teams / reports / own / specific teams. Coaching scope governs Coaching inbox and Coaching metrics; insights scope governs Team, Initiatives and Market pages.
features.gn: Deals/coaching/insights: all, manager's teams, reports, own, specific teams. Coaching = Coaching Inbox+Metrics; Insights = Team/Initiatives/Market. Forecast has view/edit/targets.
features.on: Coaching/KPI views use the same binary own-vs-company manager rule; there's no per-domain or per-team scope ladder.

features.name: Action permissions
features.what: Score calls; override scores (including AI's); view all answered scorecards regardless of visibility; download media; share calls with customers; manually schedule and upload; record on mobile; set owned calls private; trim owned calls; delete calls; delete emails.
features.gn: All 11 actions are listed (score, override incl AI, view all scorecards, download, share with customers, schedule/upload, mobile record, private, trim, delete calls, delete emails).
features.on: Overrides are manager-only via a logged RPC that requires a reason; reps can't write scores. Other actions are fixed by role, not toggles. No external share, trim or private flags.

features.name: Page access permissions
features.what: Per-page gates: Engage analytics, Conversations (search, library), Deals (create/edit/delete boards), Forecast admin, Dashboards, Accounts, Coaching, Insights, Activity, mobile Business pulse, AI Builder.
features.gn: Page gates include Engage Analytics, Conversations (Search/Library), Deals (+boards), Forecast (+manage boards), Dashboards, Account, Coaching, Insights, Activity, Business pulse, AI Builder.
features.on: Pages are gated per module by the pilot-code lock in middleware and by module membership in layouts, plus admin-only routes. These aren't per-user page toggles.

features.name: Business admin permissions
features.what: Separate grants for: general business settings, Theme Spotter analyses, tracker settings, company agents/skills/automations, AI Data Extractor, scorecards and trainings, credits, dashboards, metrics and targets.
features.gn: Business admin = general settings, Theme Spotter, Tracker, agents/skills/automations, Data Extractor, Scorecards & Trainings, credits. Dashboards, metrics and targets sit in other sections.
features.on: There's a single admin authority (C-Suite roles) and no split between tech and business admin. Rubric config writes are service-role only.

features.name: Per-call user access grants
features.what: Grant or remove an individual user's access to a specific call outside their profile scope.
features.gn: llms.txt lists API ops to give, retrieve and remove individual users' access via /v2/calls/users-access.
features.on: recording_share_events lets a manager request and the rep grant or revoke sharing a pitch as a team example (append-only, rep consent). There's no admin grant of one call to one user.

features.name: Seat-gated permissions
features.what: Some toggles only work when the user also holds the right seat (e.g. score calls needs Enable Essentials; forecast needs Gong Forecast).
features.gn: Enable Essentials gates score/override/scorecards/Coaching; Gong Forecast gates forecast; Foundation gates Deals, upload, mobile record, etc.
features.on: Features are gated by the company's module entitlement (pilot code), not by per-person seats.

features.name: Account-based permissions
features.what: Access to calls and emails tied to accounts the person can access; account access is 'assigned accounts' (own + reports' accounts + contacts), all, or none.
features.gn: Assigned accounts (owned + reports' + contacts; Salesforce Account Team counts), All, or None.
features.on: Sales Coach has no CRM account-ownership model tied to pitch visibility.

modules.name: Email & calendar capture
modules.summary: We have no calendar or mailbox integration at all: no Google/Microsoft OAuth, no calendar scan, no email sync, no exclusion lists. The closest thing is the Sales Coach Chrome extension, which reads an open Gmail/Outlook/LinkedIn/Google Voice thread on demand for coaching, not a stored timeline. Door knocks without a recording do count as activity in KPIs, which mirrors Gong's 'unrecorded meetings still count'.
modules.vsum: Claims held up well; small drift on email exclusions (admins add terms/prefixes, not clearly domains/addresses) and Exchange/LinkedIn details come from llms.txt titles and the marketing page, not the cited data-capture article.

features.name: Calendar scan to schedule recordings
features.what: After Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 is connected, Gong scans each recorded user's calendar for meetings with a conference URL. Skips: private events, meetings created less than 30 minutes before start, meetings hosted outside the company, and internal meetings when excluded.
features.gn: Skips private events, meetings scheduled <30 min ahead, externally hosted, excluded internal. Note skip-code page says OBSOLETE_CALL = within 20 min, an inconsistency in Gong's docs.
features.on: No calendar connection or scan. Grep for calendar/gmail/graph.microsoft/googleapis calendar finds only date math (salesDay.ts) and month buckets. Sessions start when the rep taps record.

features.name: Company-wide or user-by-user connection
features.what: Google Workspace and Office 365 can be connected once by an admin for everyone, or per user. Admins can restrict which mailboxes Gong may access. On-premise and cloud Exchange variants exist.
features.gn: Company-level and per-user connection confirmed on data-capture page; mailbox restriction and Exchange on-prem/cloud confirmed only as llms.txt article titles.
features.on: No OAuth mail/calendar connection of any kind, company-wide or per user.

features.name: Email import
features.what: Imports subject, body, timestamps, recipients and metadata of customer emails; shown in deal and account activity timelines.
features.gn: Data-capture page: 'Email subject and body, timestamps, recipients, and metadata' are imported.
features.on: No email sync. The Sales Coach extension reads the open Gmail/Outlook thread on demand so the rep gets coaching on it. Nothing is stored as a deal timeline.

features.name: Internal-domain list and email exclusions
features.what: Admins list internal domains (to classify calls internal/external) and configure domains, addresses and phrases that must never be imported. Public email domains and default exclusion terms ship pre-filled.
features.gn: Internal domains are confirmed. Built-in global exclude terms are confirmed. The default-terms article says admins add 'terms, prefixes', not addresses/domains. The cited recording-settings page doesn't cover email exclusions.
features.on: No internal-domain list or capture exclusion list. Grep for internal_domain/exclu in migrations found nothing relevant. Not needed until email/calendar capture exists.

features.name: Unrecorded meetings still count as activity
features.what: Meetings not recorded still appear with date, invitees and description, and count as deal activity. Private ones do not.
features.gn: Unrecorded meetings show date, invitees, description, appear in the activity timeline and count as deal activity; private calls excluded.
features.on: No calendar meetings. The door-to-door equivalent exists: a knock with no recording (even no_answer) still counts as a door knocked in the KPIs.

features.name: SMS and LinkedIn capture
features.what: Revenue Graph captures SMS (participants and body) and LinkedIn messages alongside calls and emails.
features.gn: Revenue Graph page lists 'emails, SMS, calendar events, LinkedIn messages'. The data-capture page mentions SMS but not LinkedIn.
features.on: Extension adapters read LinkedIn DMs and Google Voice (the only web route to SMS) on demand for coaching. They don't capture or store anything in the background, and native SMS is out of reach.

features.name: Digital interactions
features.what: Non-conversation buyer signals posted by partner tools: document signed, content viewed or shared, website visit, custom actions.
features.gn: Data-capture page gives doc-signed, website-view and video examples. llms.txt lists the /v2/digital-interaction and customer-engagement content viewed/shared/action APIs.
features.on: No ingestion of buyer digital signals and no inbound partner API.

modules.name: Web-conference recording
modules.summary: We have no meeting bot, no Zoom/Meet/Teams recording import and no recording-rule engine. Our capture is always rep-initiated through the device mic (live session, Meeting Coach, door recorder), so call-owner rules and auto-record settings mostly do not apply. We partly have honest 'why wasn't this analysed' handling: pitch failure statuses, curated failure messages and capture-gap detection. There is no closed skip-code list.
modules.vsum: Nearly every claim was confirmed verbatim. Two exceptions: owner 'host matched by name' is not stated, and the intro's 'fifty-plus skip codes' undercounts (81 total).

features.name: Recording bot joins meetings
features.what: A virtual participant joins the meeting and records audio (and optionally video). Bot display name is selectable: 'Gong Recorder', '[Company] Recorder by Gong', 'Gong AI Notetaker', 'Gong Notetaker'.
features.gn: Recorder joins as a participant; the four display names are confirmed verbatim on define-the-recording-settings.
features.on: No recording bot. Meeting Coach captures through the device mic (getUserMedia). The Teams adapter in the extension reads chat text only. Searched tabCapture/offscreen/MediaRecorder in the extensions and found none.

features.name: Native Zoom recording import
features.what: Zoom records in-platform; Gong retrieves the file afterwards. No bot appears. ON AIR shows ~15 minutes before (5 for back-to-back on a personal room) until end, up to 6 hours after scheduled end.
features.gn: No recorder in native Zoom mode; ON AIR ~15 min before (5 for back-to-back personal room), up to 6 h after scheduled end.
features.on: No Zoom integration or recording.completed webhook. A rep can export a Zoom file and upload it manually.

features.name: Supported providers
features.what: Zoom, Google Meet, Webex, Microsoft Teams, GoToMeeting, Amazon Chime, RingCentral Meetings/Video, join.me, Uber Conference, Appointlet; admin chooses which providers to record.
features.gn: Consent article lists Zoom, Meet, WebEx, Teams, GoToMeeting, Chime, RingCentral Meetings/Video, join.me, Uber Conference, Appointlet; 'Set the providers to record' is in llms.txt.
features.on: No conferencing-provider integrations. A video call can only be coached if the laptop mic hears it, or by uploading a file afterwards.

features.name: Company recording rules
features.what: Which meetings to record (organised by a recorded member, or organised by anyone with a recorded member invited); record internal calls yes/no; audio+video or audio only; minimum duration to import (default 30 s; 3 s fixed for Gong Dialer). Per-member settings override company settings.
features.gn: Two 'which meetings' options, internal yes/no, audio+video vs audio, 30 s default min (3 s Gong Dialer, not configurable), individual settings override.
features.on: No auto-record rules because nothing records automatically. The rep presses record. The per-rep Macro Mode toggle only switches the door-to-door UI on or off. There is no minimum-duration import threshold.

features.name: Per-member data capture setting
features.what: Each team member has a data capture setting; 'Never record' on any participant blocks recording even if the bot is invited.
features.gn: 'Never record' on any team member blocks recording even with the recorder invited (HAS_DO_NOT_RECORD_USERS).
features.on: No per-member capture mode. There is no ambient capture, so recording happens only when the rep starts it.

features.name: Manual 'record now' and scheduled recording
features.what: Invite the recorder or use Home > More actions > Schedule new recording with a URL. 'Now' can take up to ten minutes to start. Users can stop or cancel from Home.
features.gn: Schedule new recording plus the 'up to ten minutes' claim is confirmed. Stop/cancel isn't on that page; the skip codes CANCELED_BY_OWNER / STOP_USER_REQUEST ('stopped via the homepage') support it.
features.on: Record-now is our only mode and starts instantly in-app (live session / door recorder). The auto-close-stale cron ends abandoned sessions. Nothing gets scheduled ahead of time.

features.name: Six-hour cap
features.what: Recording and processing is limited to six hours; longer calls skip with TOO_LONG.
features.gn: 'Gong cannot process recordings longer than six hours'; TOO_LONG skip code.
features.on: We cap uploads by size (25 MB AGENT_MAX_BYTES), not by duration. Door pitches upload in ~15 s chunks, so a long pitch survives. There's no explicit TOO_LONG reason shown to the user.

features.name: Call owner resolution
features.what: Before the call, first match wins: scheduled via Gong Home → meeting URL on a member's profile → provider API says whose URL → organizer is a recorded member → invited recorded member (most recorded calls wins). After: planned owner attended → else host matched by name (or screen-sharer) → else an attending member; with several, planned owner keeps it. Recalculated if the event changes.
features.gn: Pre-call order and post-call rules confirmed; recalculated if event changes; owner editable. Article says 'recorded member hosted', not 'host matched by name'.
features.on: Owner is always the rep who recorded (session agent_id / pitch rep_id). There's no multi-participant ownership problem to solve.

features.name: Skip codes for unrecorded calls
features.what: Every unrecorded meeting gets a reason code: e.g. BAD_SCHEDULE, CALL_BLOCKLISTED, COMPLIANCE_USER_REQUEST, DENIED_ENTRY, HAS_DO_NOT_RECORD_USERS, INTERNAL_MEETING, MEETING_LOCKED, NO_ATTENDEES, NO_COMPANY_PARTICIPANTS, OBSOLETE_CALL (organised within 20 min), PASSWORD_REQUIRED, TOO_LONG, TOO_SHORT, WEB_CLIENT_DISABLED, plus meeting-level codes (ALL_DAY_EVENT, NO_URL, PRIVATE_OR_CONFIDENTIAL, NO_CRM_MATCH) and dialer codes (BUSY_LINE, CARRIER_BLOCKED, RECORDING_RESTRICTED).
features.gn: All named codes present; page has 81 codes (10 dialer, 56 web conference, 15 meeting). OBSOLETE_CALL = within 20 min confirmed.
features.on: pitch_status 'failed' plus curated rep-facing reasons (no audio, no speech, timeout, AI unavailable) and capture-gap classification. No closed, reportable reason-code table or status report.

features.name: Leave if no company participant
features.what: If nobody from the company joins, the bot leaves and discards the recording (NO_COMPANY_PARTICIPANTS); if nobody joins at all, NO_ATTENDEES.
features.gn: NO_COMPANY_PARTICIPANTS: bot leaves and discards its portion; NO_ATTENDEES when nobody else joins.
features.on: No bot to leave. The closest analogue: we detect one-sided capture (agent-missing / customer-missing) and no-speech recordings, then auto-recover or flag them instead of analysing.

features.name: Live insights inside Zoom
features.what: A Gong app inside Zoom shows insights during the call. Basis: articles 'Gong live insights for Zoom' and 'About the Gong app for Zoom' in index; content not read.
features.gn: Article exists: Live Insights streams the live transcript and shows tips in the Gong App for Zoom side panel; BETA, invite-only, paid Zoom, never records.
features.on: We deliver live in-call coaching cues in our own app (LiveCoachingPanel, realtime token), not inside Zoom. Arguably further along for in-person and phone calls.

modules.name: Telephony, dialer imports, mobile & uploads
modules.summary: Our main capture paths match Gong's mobile recording: in-browser door-pitch recording with chunked upload, outcomes per knock and a processing status, plus manual file upload with diarization and a 'which voice is you' speaker label. We have no telephony or dialer import, no Salesforce fallback, no virtual numbers and no public create-call API. Upload is capped at 25 MB, against Gong's 2 GB. A full offline queue is built but switched off.
modules.vsum: Claims were mostly confirmed. Exceptions: Gong Connect is a VoIP dialer in the app that uses the rep's own mobile number, not clearly 'virtual numbers', and Recents is documented as showing upload status only.

features.name: Telephony API import
features.what: Connects to provider APIs (8x8, Aircall, Dialpad, RingCentral, Twilio Flex, Zoom Phone, Talkdesk, Five9, Genesys, Outreach, Salesloft, HubSpot and ~20 more) and downloads recordings plus call attempts, including calls without recordings. Recording must be on in the telephony system and the user set to import.
features.gn: 32 API-integrated providers (39 unique across all methods). Requires recording enabled in telephony and users set to import. 'Calls without recordings' is stated on data-capture, not the telephony page.
features.on: No telephony integration. Grep for twilio/aircall/dialpad/ringcentral/dialer across src and migrations returned nothing. Phone calls are coached live through the mic or uploaded as a file.

features.name: Import via Salesforce activities
features.what: For some dialers, Gong finds recordings through Salesforce activities the dialer creates after each call.
features.gn: 8 dialers via Salesforce integration (ConnectAndSell, Conquer, groove, Xant, SF Lightning, SalesLoft, Talkdesk, ringDNA); requires Salesforce connection.
features.on: No CRM or Salesforce integration.

features.name: Manual file upload
features.what: Upload WAV, MP3, MP4, MKV or FLAC up to 2 GB from the quick-actions menu or Conversations > Search. Analysis takes up to an hour; user can rename, make private or delete while processing; email on completion. Uploaded calls have no participant metadata; speakers are named afterwards.
features.gn: WAV/MP3/MP4/MKV/FLAC, 2 GB, quick actions or Conversations > Search, up to 1 h, rename/private/delete while processing, email when done, no metadata.
features.on: Upload accepts many audio/video formats, uploads directly to storage, then diarizes with a one-tap speaker label. Missing: the cap is 25 MB (Gong allows 2 GB) and there's no completion email.

features.name: In-person recording on mobile
features.what: Gong app > Actions > Record a meeting. Meetings starting within 2 hours are offered for linking, or SKIP to record unlinked. Record/pause/resume, stop, name, optionally link account/opportunity/contacts, save; then upload, analyse, transcribe. Audio only. Needs 'manually schedule & upload' permission.
features.gn: Actions > Record a meeting, meetings within 2 h, RECORD/SKIP, pause/resume, link account/opp/contacts (contacts iOS only), audio only, 'Manually schedule and upload' permission.
features.on: Door Log is our main capture path: tap to record a pitch in the mobile web app, ~15 s chunks upload during recording, wake lock, and each pitch is tied to a knock. No calendar linking and no visible pause.

features.name: Background recording indicator (iOS Live Activity)
features.what: On supported iPhones a Live Activity shows recording status and elapsed time while the app is backgrounded or the phone is locked; tapping returns to the recording.
features.gn: iOS Live Activity shows recording status and elapsed time while backgrounded or locked; tap returns to the recording.
features.on: We're a web app, so there's no lock-screen indicator. We hold a screen wake lock (often refused on iOS) and warn the rep when the mic track ends.

features.name: Recents with upload and analysis status
features.what: The mobile Recents tab shows each recent recording's upload and analysis state.
features.gn: Recents tab shows 'upload status of recent recordings' and lets you act on them; analysis state isn't explicitly stated on the page.
features.on: Pitch status enum is recorded/uploading/transcribing/analyzing/complete/failed. The UI collapses it to 'processing…' or 'processing failed', so the stages are not shown as chips.

features.name: Call outcomes after a mobile recording
features.what: After a call the rep adds a call outcome to track the result and plan follow-ups.
features.gn: 'Add call outcomes after the call to track results and plan follow-ups'; GET /v2/call-outcomes listed in llms.txt.
features.on: Every knock has an outcome: no_answer, sold, go_back, non_decision_maker or not_interested. These feed the KPI tiles directly. The list is fixed (no custom outcomes).

features.name: Mobile phone calls via Gong Connect
features.what: Virtual phone numbers that let reps' mobile calls be captured. Basis: data-capture article lists 'Gong Connect: virtual phone numbers for the Gong dialer'; 'Capture mobile calls with Gong Connect' article not read.
features.gn: Article exists: Gong Connect is a VoIP mobile dialer in the app. Outbound uses the rep's personal mobile number as caller ID by default; virtual/business numbers only for Engage users. Only in-app calls are recorded.
features.on: No dialer or phone-number provisioning.

features.name: Create call via API with media
features.what: External systems create a call record then attach media.
features.gn: llms.txt lists 'Add new call' (POST /v2/calls) and 'Add call media' (/v2/calls/{id}/media).
features.on: No public or partner API. Searched src/app/api for a v1/API-key surface and found only user-session routes.

features.name: Offline-safe recording
features.what: Gong's mobile article says nothing about recording without signal or resuming failed uploads. Field reps lose signal. Proposal: record to local storage first, upload in chunks when online, never lose a session.
features.gn: Absence holds: the mobile article doesn't cover offline recording, signal loss or upload retry. The App Store listing mentions only explanations for failed uploads plus re-upload/export.
features.on: Chunks upload during recording, and saves retry with backoff. A full IndexedDB offline queue (client_knock_id dedupe) is built and tested but deliberately switched off since 2026-08-18.

modules.name: Recording consent
modules.summary: We have none of Gong's consent machinery: no consent profiles, announcements, consent page, opt-out, pre-call email or opt-out reporting. For in-person door recording, the founder decided on 2026-08-18 that consent is 'legally handled' with no in-flow gate. The privacy page tells reps they must record lawfully. The only 'consent' table we have covers managers sharing recordings, not recording itself.
modules.vsum: Every Gong consent claim was confirmed close to verbatim. The one gap: dialer rules are described per 'region', not per country/area code.

features.name: Consent profiles assigned by team
features.what: Multiple profiles, each assigned to teams or regions; stricter rule applies when participants are in different regions.
features.gn: Profiles per team (and per provider/branding/subsidiary/language); 'the stricter consent law generally applies' across locations.
features.on: No consent profiles or per-team recording policy.

features.name: Audio announcement
features.what: A prompt plays when participants join; per participant or once; language, voice and text configurable; can be skipped for people who already consented on the consent page. Phone calls require a verbal notice.
features.gn: Prompt per participant or once; language, voice and text configurable; skip if already consented; integrated telephony requires a verbal notice.
features.on: No recording announcement. We have TTS (sales-session/tts) but it isn't used for consent.

features.name: Hosted consent page, enabled or enforced
features.what: Meeting links redirect to a branded consent page. Enabled: bypassers may still be recorded. Enforced: recorded only if all participants consent. Localised to browser language.
features.gn: Enabled vs Enforced confirmed; logo/company/text branding; browser-language localization, default English; no page from room systems.
features.on: No consent page. Not applicable to door-to-door as built.

features.name: Join without recording (opt-out)
features.what: Participants can decline and still join; the call is not recorded (skip code COMPLIANCE_USER_REQUEST). Not available on every provider.
features.gn: Opt-out on Chime, Meet, GoToMeeting, Teams, RingCentral, WebEx, Zoom; not on Appointlet, join.me, Uber Conference. Skip code COMPLIANCE_USER_REQUEST.
features.on: No participant opt-out. The prospect has no in-product way to decline.

features.name: Pre-call recording email
features.what: Sent 10–20 minutes before the meeting; subject, body, logo and privacy link customisable; the recording notice itself cannot be removed.
features.gn: Sent 10-20 min before from Gong's email service; subject, body, logo, privacy policy customizable; the recording notice can't be removed or edited.
features.on: No pre-call email (and no calendar to drive one).

features.name: Dynamic vs static meeting links
features.what: Dynamic links (per meeting, via calendar add-on) are most secure but don't support personal rooms or Calendly; static links support those but need setup.
features.gn: Dynamic: per-meeting via calendar add-on, most secure, no PMR/Calendly/on-behalf (Zoom/Meet/Teams/WebEx). Static: supports Calendly and on-behalf, risk of overlapping recordings.
features.on: Not applicable. We have no meeting-link interception.

features.name: Opt-out rate reporting
features.what: The Call status report shows how many participants opted out.
features.gn: 'You can track opt-outs with the Call status report.'
features.on: No opt-out data, so no opt-out reporting.

features.name: Country and area-code recording restrictions (dialer)
features.what: For dialer calls, recording can be auto, manual-only or prohibited per country or area code.
features.gn: Skip codes AUTO_RECORDING_EXCLUDED / MANUAL_RECORDING_EXCLUDED / RECORDING_RESTRICTED describe per-REGION auto/manual/prohibited. Country/area-code granularity isn't stated.
features.on: No dialer and no jurisdiction-based recording rules.

features.name: Consent capture for in-person sessions
features.what: Gong's mobile recording article gives no consent guidance for in-person meetings. A door-to-door session records a homeowner who never saw a consent page. Proposal: a required consent step before recording starts (rep taps 'customer agreed', optionally records the verbal yes as the first seconds of audio).
features.gn: Absence holds: the mobile article has no consent guidance. The consent doc routes mobile calls to separate Gong Connect privacy articles and admits room systems bypass the consent page.
features.on: Founder chose 'consent legally handled, NO in-flow gate' (2026-08-18). The privacy page makes reps responsible for lawful recording. The door state machine has a slot for adding a CONSENT state later.

modules.name: Transcription, speakers & language
modules.summary: We transcribe and diarize every session (ElevenLabs Scribe, 2 speakers, versioned append-only segments) and identify the rep via a mandatory pitch-based voice enrollment plus one-tap fallback. We lack everything multilingual (STT pinned to English, no translation, no UI locales) and custom vocabulary.
modules.vsum: Gong's speaker, language, translation and vocabulary claims all held up almost verbatim; only F8.1 lacked a timestamp statement in its cited article.

features.name: Transcription
features.what: Every recorded call is transcribed with timestamps per segment.
features.gn: web-conference article confirms a transcript after processing but no timestamps; API /v2/calls/transcript listed in llms.txt; explore-call-content confirms click-to-seek lines.
features.on: Every session is transcribed by ElevenLabs Scribe (live + batch), stored as append-only, versioned, timed segments; a retranscribe route recovers sessions whose transcript never landed.

features.name: Diarization by recording type
features.what: Conference and mono calls are split by voice differences, with a second pass for short utterances; stereo phone calls treat each channel as one speaker.
features.gn: Conference: split by voice variance + refinement for short utterances; stereo: one speaker per channel; mono: split by voice variance.
features.on: Scribe diarizes into 2 speaker clusters (stored as speaker_cluster) and a live pitch (F0) clusterer separates voices; only agent/customer/unknown roles, no multi-party or stereo-channel path.

features.name: Speaker-to-person matching
features.what: Conference speakers are matched by display name (full or unique short forms) or phone number to invitees; stereo phone: one channel to the Gong user, the other to the external party; mono phone: transcript decides which side is the company, voice ID as fallback. Shared Zoom rooms become 'Speaker 1/2'.
features.gn: Name/short-name/phone matching for conference, channel-to-user for stereo, transcript then voice ID for mono, Zoom shared rooms as Speaker 1/2 — all stated.
features.on: We only need 'which voice is the rep': auto-assign by overlap with live agent turns plus enrolled pitch, declining when unsure and falling back to a one-tap 'which voice is you?' card. No contact matching.

features.name: Voice identification for opted-in users
features.what: Admin enables, each user opts in. Up to five short samples (ideally mono calls with 2+ minutes of speech), continually replaced. Once enough exist, earlier calls are re-analysed. No voice data for non-users; no voice-print file retained.
features.gn: Admin enables, user opts in, up to 5 samples ideally mono 2+ min, continually replaced, earlier calls reanalysed, no file retained. Also: works from 2nd call.
features.on: Voice enrollment is a mandatory gate, not opt-in: rep reads a prompt once and we store one median pitch number (Hz), never audio. No rolling samples, no re-analysis of past sessions.

features.name: Rename speakers on the call page
features.what: A participant or admin edits speaker names (documented for Zoom-native and uploaded calls).
features.gn: Zoom shared-room speakers renamable by participant or business admin; uploaded-call speakers renamable with permissions; call page lets you fix names in Call Info.
features.on: Rep can flip/assign roles (rep vs customer) via label-transcript and attribute-unlabelled (relabel RPC appends a new version). No free-text speaker names or person linking.

features.name: 70+ languages with auto-detection
features.what: 72 language entries (71 distinct), including Filipino (Philippines). Language detected automatically; if wrong, users set spoken languages in My Profile and reprocess.
features.gn: 72 entries / 71 distinct incl. Filipino (Philippines); auto-detect; fix via spoken languages in My Profile + reprocess. No mention of code-switching/Taglish.
features.on: STT is pinned to English ('eng') on purpose because auto-detect mislabeled accented English; no per-user or per-tenant language setting.

features.name: English-only features
features.what: Email labels, red-flag alerts, Gong-recommended to-dos and example-based smart trackers are English only; question-based smart trackers work in all languages; Gong Assistant answers in the question's language.
features.gn: Email labels, red-flag alerts, recommended to-dos, example-based smart trackers English-only; question-based trackers all languages; Assistant answers in question's language.
features.on: Not applicable as a gap: the whole product is English-only today, so every feature is effectively English-only.

features.name: AI translation of transcripts and briefs
features.what: Transcripts, summaries and call/contact/account/deal briefs translate from any language; per-source-language auto-translate preference or on demand; admin defaults; translated summaries can export to CRM.
features.gn: AI Translator for transcripts, summaries, call/contact/account/deal briefs; per-source-language auto-translate or on demand; admin defaults; CRM export.
features.on: No translation of transcripts or summaries anywhere (searched 'translat' across coach code; only prompt wording hits).

features.name: Custom vocabulary
features.what: Per-workspace terms with classification (our company / another company / general) and comma-separated mis-transcriptions per language. Applies to new calls immediately and to history within hours; only transcript text changes, AI outputs are not regenerated.
features.gn: Classification (our company/another company/general), comma-separated mis-transcriptions per language, new calls immediately, history within hours, AI outputs not regenerated.
features.on: No STT custom vocabulary or keyterm list (grepped keyterm/custom_vocab). src/lib/coach/vocabulary.ts is a negative-phrasing heuristic library, not transcription correction.

features.name: UI language
features.what: Interface in English, French, Canadian French and Korean; rolling out.
features.gn: UI languages English, Francais, Francais Canadien, Korean; rolling out progressively.
features.on: UI is English-only; no i18n library or locale picker (layout locale hard-coded en_US).

modules.name: Call page, player & collaboration
modules.summary: We have a manager Recordings player (speed, skip, waveform with scored-moment markers, playhead transcript), timestamped manager-to-rep comments, rename, processing states and audio-only delete. We lack speaker isolation/talk-time lanes, transcript search, snippets, external/embed sharing, downloads, listen-later, trim and in-call notes; sharing is deliberately consent-gated instead.
modules.vsum: Nearly all call-page claims confirmed; trim restore window is inconsistent in Gong's own article, hashtags come only from a different article, and the INFERRED notes feature is now confirmed.

features.name: Processing state on the call page
features.what: While media is prepared the page shows 'Processing call media'; briefs, transcript and playback appear when done.
features.gn: 'Processing call media' shown; briefs, transcript, playback appear when done; transcript can precede video.
features.on: Door pitches show processing / processing-failed states with 'analysis will appear shortly'; sessions list shows processing; score panel has explicit scoring/failed states.

features.name: Player with speaker isolation
features.what: Skip ±15 s, playback speed, isolate one speaker's sections, scrub the timeline to jump.
features.gn: Skip back/forward 15 s, playback speed, isolate individual speakers, scrub timeline.
features.on: Recordings tab player: play/pause, skip 10 s, speeds 1-2x, waveform scrub. No per-speaker isolation; player only on manager Recordings tab, not on the session page.

features.name: Talk-time bar
features.what: Bar under the player showing when each participant spoke; pick a participant to listen only to them.
features.gn: Talk-time bar below the player shows when each participant spoke; lets you listen to one participant.
features.on: Our timeline strip marks scored moments (missed/bonus/pattern/comment), not who spoke when. No speaker lanes.

features.name: Transcript panel with search
features.what: Speaker-attributed text; click a line to seek; in-panel search highlights matches. Translated transcripts aren't searchable.
features.gn: Click line to jump; search bar highlights matches; translated transcripts not searchable.
features.on: Session page shows full speaker-labelled transcript (Expert mode); Recordings tab highlights the line at the playhead. No in-transcript search; click-to-seek only via key moments.

features.name: AI outline
features.what: AI-generated timestamped section summary; click a heading to jump.
features.gn: AI-generated summary split into timestamped sections; click heading to jump.
features.on: We generate a factual conversation summary plus a 3-5 key-moment timeline (After-Pitch) rather than a sectioned outline; recordings' key moments are click-to-seek.

features.name: Call info and points of interest
features.what: Attendees, date, duration, classification, CRM associations; correct speaker names; manual CRM association. Points of interest auto-flag questions asked, competitor mentions, pricing discussions and filler words as timeline markers.
features.gn: Attendees, date, duration, classification, speaker-name fix, manual CRM association, and POIs (questions, competitors, pricing, filler) confirmed; separate CRM-associations list not mentioned.
features.on: Session header shows client label, date, duration, context (in-person/video). Markers are rubric moments (missed/bonus/pattern), not questions/competitor/pricing/filler flags. No CRM link.

features.name: Rename call and edit details
features.what: Click the title to rename; edit participant details in Call Info.
features.gn: Click the call title to rename; edit participant details on Call Info tab.
features.on: Sessions are named (clientLabel) at end-of-call and renamable via PATCH from the session and After-Pitch pages.

features.name: Timestamped comments with mentions and visibility
features.what: Comment on a moment; @mention colleagues (they're notified and see it under Home > Collaboration > Received, plus email/Slack per settings); visibility: everyone, specific people, or only me; edit/delete. Hashtags are searchable.
features.gn: Timestamped comments, @mentions -> Received in Collaboration, email/Slack per settings, visibility (everyone/specific/only me), edit/delete all confirmed. Hashtags only in introduction-to-coaching.
features.on: Managers leave timestamped comments on a pitch; 'Save and send to rep' notifies the rep. Append-only by design (no edit/delete), no @mentions, no visibility levels beyond draft vs sent, no hashtags.

features.name: Host performance stats in side panel
features.what: Right panel shows the call host's talk ratio and longest monologue for this call.
features.gn: Collaboration panel shows host stats: talk ratio and longest monologue.
features.on: After-Pitch score strip shows talk/listen ratio and question rate per session. No longest-monologue stat.

features.name: Share internally
features.what: Share with colleagues plus a message; they get a notification and need an account to view.
features.gn: Share internally with optional message; recipients notified; need a Gong account.
features.on: No ad-hoc share. Instead a manager can request 'save as team example' and only the rep can grant/decline/revoke (consent event log). Nothing yet plays granted clips to other reps.

features.name: Share with customers by link
features.what: Customer-facing link for the full call or a snippet; admin caps expiry at up to 100 days; 'anyone with link' (identity via Google or LinkedIn) or 'only specific people' from approved domains after email verification; full-call shares can include Highlights and Outline.
features.gn: Full call or snippet; admin max 100 days; anyone-with-link via Google/LinkedIn or specific people from approved domains; Highlights+Outline for full calls.
features.on: No external/customer share links or public routes; recordings are company-RLS only.

features.name: Shares & views tracking
features.what: For external shares, a Shares & Views tab lists share details and view activity.
features.gn: Shares & Views tab in right panel shows share details and view activity for external shares.
features.on: No view tracking (no external shares exist).

features.name: Snippets
features.what: Drag yellow bars to select a portion; share, comment, save to library, download or embed the snippet. Recipients see only that part; original untouched.
features.gn: Drag yellow bars; share, comment, save to library, download, embed, request feedback, trim; recipients see only the portion.
features.on: No clip/snippet creation; comments pin a second but cannot carve a portion.

features.name: Embed a call
features.what: Embed code for internal wikis (viewer must be signed in and permitted); 'copy embed link' for non-users gives the player without transcript or summaries.
features.gn: Embed code for signed-in permitted members; 'copy embed link' for non-users gives player without transcript/summaries.
features.on: No embed route or embed code.

features.name: Download audio, video or transcript
features.what: Download media or transcript; needs 'Download call media'.
features.gn: Download audio, video or transcript; needs 'Download call media' permission.
features.on: No audio or transcript download from session/recording pages (only KPI CSV exports exist).

features.name: Listen later and add to library
features.what: Top-right actions save the call to 'Listen later' or a library folder.
features.gn: Top-right actions: Add to library, save to Listen later.
features.on: No bookmark/listen-later or call library. Strategy Library holds methodology + the rep's own 'correct lines', not recordings.

features.name: Trim with six-month restore
features.what: Owner or tech admin trims a section; it disappears from playback, transcript and AI outputs after reprocessing. Original restorable within six months of the recording date (triggers reanalysis). Existing customer links are not revoked.
features.gn: Owner/tech admin trim, removal from playback/transcript/AI, reanalysis, links not revoked confirmed; page contradicts itself: 6 months from recording date vs from trimming.
features.on: No trim. Audio can only be removed whole (delete-recording) or by the retention purge cron.

features.name: Permanent delete
features.what: Removes recording, transcript, comments, scores, notes, stats, related tasks and the CRM conversation record. No recovery. Bulk delete is tech-admin only.
features.gn: Removes recording, transcript, comments, scores, notes, stats, tasks, Salesforce record; no recovery; bulk delete Tech admins only.
features.on: Managers/admins (not reps) can delete a recording's AUDIO only; transcript, scores and notes are kept on purpose so skill history isn't rewritten. No full-session hard delete.

features.name: Set a call private
features.what: Restrict access without removing content; owners need 'set owned calls as private'.
features.gn: Privacy restricts access without removing content (confirmed); permission is 'Set calls they own as private' per permission page; effect on stats not stated.
features.on: No per-call private toggle. Sessions are private by RLS by default (owner + same-company manager); After-Pitch scores are rep-only; peer visibility only through consent-gated team examples.

features.name: Take notes during a call
features.what: Reps take notes during a recorded call that attach to it. Basis: 'Take notes during a call' article in index; content not read.
features.gn: Article now exists (updated 2026-01-06): notepad in homepage Conversations widget during live call; notes post timestamped to the call's comments; pushed to Salesforce with task.
features.on: Reps can't type notes during a session; the door log captures outcome taps and the session page has outcome fields, not timestamped notes.

modules.name: Interaction stats & team insights
modules.summary: We compute talk ratio (by words) and question share per session, plus duration/volume KPIs, rubric scorecards per rep and pattern clustering. We lack Gong's timing-based mechanics (longest monologue, customer story, interactivity, patience) and category-split team stats.
modules.vsum: Benchmarks and definitions confirmed exactly; minor drift on call-category rule sources, Whisper's description, and scorecard plan availability.

features.name: Talk ratio
features.what: Share of the call the rep speaks; computed per call then averaged. Benchmark ~43% rep for top-converting B2B calls.
features.gn: Share of the call rep talks; 43:57 (rep:customer) cited as highest-converting B2B ratio.
features.on: We compute talk ratio from WORD counts (not speech time) per session, with a capture-gap caveat and our own bands (>=75% rep flagged). Team rollup via talk_listen skill score.

features.name: Longest monologue
features.what: Longest uninterrupted rep stretch per call; benchmark ≤2:30.
features.gn: Longest uninterrupted rep stretch; aim for 2:30 or less.
features.on: No longest-monologue stat. The AT&T rubric only mentions '~90 s monologue' as a trigger description for the LLM grader.

features.name: Longest customer story
features.what: Longest uninterrupted customer stretch; shows whether they could share needs. Company-level stat (same for everyone on the call).
features.gn: Longest customer stretch; same number for all company participants on the call.
features.on: No longest-customer-story stat.

features.name: Interactivity score
features.what: How often speech switches between company and external side, counted per 5-minute block and averaged; capped at 10; brief acknowledgements don't count; benchmark ≥5. Only calls scoring 1–10 with talk ratio 1–99% are included.
features.gn: Switches per 5-min block, averaged, capped 10, acknowledgements excluded, aim >=5, included only if score 1-10 and talk ratio 1-99%.
features.on: No interactivity/turn-switch metric (grepped interactivity).

features.name: Patience
features.what: Rep's pause after the customer stops before responding; median per call, then averaged; benchmark 0.6–1.0 s.
features.gn: Median pause before rep speaks after customer stops, averaged; aim 0.6-1 s.
features.on: No response-latency metric; segments carry spoken_at timing that could support it.

features.name: Question rate
features.what: Rep questions scaled to an hour; benchmark ≥18/hour.
features.gn: Questions per hour scaled from call length, aim 18+, confirmed. Artifact omits nothing material.
features.on: Our question rate is the share of rep TURNS that are questions (e.g. '6 of 20'), heuristic '?'/interrogative opener detection; not per hour.

features.name: Activity stats
features.what: Average call duration, weekly call volume, weekly hours on calls, total call volume and total time per person in period.
features.gn: Avg call duration, weekly call volume, weekly hours on calls, total volume and total time for period.
features.on: KPI page has sessions per day and avg session duration (known-duration only), plus door counts. No weekly hours-on-calls or total time.

features.name: Email responsiveness stats
features.what: Fast team response (% answered within 24 h), team response time (excl. >7 days), team response rate (% within 7 days); auto-replies and thank-yous excluded.
features.gn: Fast team response (24 h), response time (excl. >7 days), response rate (7 days); auto-replies/thank-yous excluded; not on Call Essentials.
features.on: No email capture in Sales Coach; not relevant to door/phone reps.

features.name: Team page controls
features.what: Pick a manager's team or several teams/members, period and call category; toggle Individuals (row per person) and Attended (include calls joined, not just hosted); click a row for that person.
features.gn: Manager or multiple teams/members, period, call category, Individuals and Attended toggles all confirmed.
features.on: Manager boards (Coach Assessment reps table, KPI team, team analytics) give per-rep rows; sessions list filters by context/status/period. No team picker, category filter or 'attended' toggle on stats.

features.name: Call categories
features.what: Calls are classified (e.g. discovery, demo); stats filtered by category because norms differ by stage.
features.gn: Categories exist and filter Team page; defined by Search-page field filters (CRM stages, teams). Rules on title/participants and discovery/demo examples not in source.
features.on: Sessions carry context (in_person|video) and session_kind (sales|meeting|huddle); sales-only filtering is applied, but stats aren't split by category.

features.name: Topic and tracker share per team
features.what: % of calls covering each topic (needs ≥4 calls else N/A), time per topic, and % of calls where each tracker fired.
features.gn: Topic needs >=4 calls else N/A; tracker % of calls; admin chooses trackers; AI trackers English-only.
features.on: No topic/tracker share. We cluster 'why' patterns and Pattern Interrupt across a rep's calls instead of keyword trackers.

features.name: Scorecards tab on Team page
features.what: How each scorecard scores across the team; drill to a question for per-person detail; private scorecards excluded. Needs Enable Essentials.
features.gn: Scorecard by team, drill to question per person, private excluded confirmed; available on Enable Essentials AND Enable (artifact says needs Enable Essentials).
features.on: Coach Assessment board shows each rep's rubric (pitch score) results and six /10 skill grades with per-rep drill-in; rubric sections from one config.

features.name: Whisper: recommendations from top performers
features.what: Automatic coaching recommendations comparing each member to best practice for interaction stats; business admin defines the call filter set. Whisper for Topics has been retired.
features.gn: Managing-whisper confirms automatic recommendations, business-admin filter, Data studio location; best-practice comparison per member not stated; Topics retirement is in a separate article.
features.on: No top-performer benchmark engine. A Team Training Brief LLM pools the team's own growth areas (gated by a minimum dissect count) for the manager's next meeting.

features.name: Field-session stats
features.what: Gong's stats assume seated calls. A door session has different mechanics: time to first question, time to pitch, objection count, ask-for-the-close count. Proposal: a second stat set for in-person sessions, without benchmarks until your own data sets them.
features.gn: Stats page has no in-person stats and says stats cover recorded calls; but Gong's mobile app does record face-to-face meetings (record-meetings-on-mobile), so the gap is stats, not capture.
features.on: Field stats exist differently: door log counts (doors/presentations/sold), AT&T rubric sections incl. discovery and close scored per pitch. No time-to-first-question, time-to-pitch or close-attempt counts.

modules.name: Trackers & topics
modules.summary: We have no configurable trackers. What we have instead is a fixed, versioned pitch rubric (per company) that grades every element hit/partial/missed with a quote and a playable timestamp, plus an LLM pass that pulls out competitors and 3-5 topics per call. There are no admin-written keyword or question trackers, no preview/backfill workflow for them, no tracker search filters, and no continuous topic timeline.
modules.vsum: All 12 claims held up against Gong's help pages. Two small nuances: the 'side' picker exists only in the free-text path, and download/upload is documented in the copy-trackers article, not in About trackers.

features.name: Keyword trackers
features.what: Exact words/phrases (competitors, products, required disclosures) on calls and emails; active on save; no credits; downloadable/uploadable.
features.gn: About trackers: calls+emails, active on save, no credits. CSV download/upload is in the copy-keyword-trackers article, not About trackers.
features.on: There are no admin-defined phrase lists. The nearest thing is the LLM intel pass, which names competitors generically from the call and does not use a configured list.

features.name: AI trackers (question-based)
features.what: Natural-language detection question; guided builder (three phrase sections + details) or free text; choose side: our rep / customer / any party; warns on similar existing tracker; works in all languages.
features.gn: Guided builder (3 phrase sections) or free text; similar-tracker warning; all languages. The side choice (rep/customer/any) is on the free-text path only.
features.on: Rubric elements work like fixed AI trackers: the LLM grades each one hit/partial/missed with evidence and a timestamp. The rubric lives as versioned rubric_config data, but users cannot write their own detection questions.

features.name: Tracker scope and partial-call window
features.what: Calls or calls+emails; filters by call type, deal stage, participants; restrict to the first or last part of a call by minutes or percent.
features.gn: Scope is calls or calls+emails; Edit filters covers call type, deal stage and participants; the window is anytime/first/last portion by minutes or %.
features.on: No per-detector scope filters and no partial-call window. Rubric sections (intro/discovery/close) group elements by meaning, not by position in the call.

features.name: Preview against a sample
features.what: Test on 100 calls and 400 email threads; open matches with summary and snippet; iterate; save as draft (no credits).
features.gn: Preview runs on 100 calls and 400 email threads; drafts show a Draft label and use no credits.
features.on: No way to preview a detector against a sample of past calls, and no draft state.

features.name: Start/end dates and backfill
features.what: Past start date backfills history (queued after publish); future start = Scheduled; end date pauses it. Edits apply going forward; past results kept.
features.gn: A future start date makes it Scheduled, a past one backfills, an end date sets Paused; edits apply going forward and past results are kept.
features.on: Rubric versions are pinned per score (never edited in place) and there is a pitch-score backfill route, so history stays explainable. There are no start/end dates or scheduling.

features.name: Credit estimate blocks publish
features.what: Publish shows estimated credit cost; blocked if credits don't cover it; trackers pause when credits run out and must be republished.
features.gn: create-ai-trackers: publish is blocked if credits don't cover the estimate. About trackers: published AI trackers auto-pause when credits run out and need a manual republish.
features.on: No credit system or cost estimate. LLM spend is bounded by rate limits and engine timeouts, not a credit balance. The 'quota' route is a deals-won sales target, unrelated.

features.name: Pre-built 'AI trackers by Gong'
features.what: Pricing, objections, risk signals etc.; activate only; not editable; no credits.
features.gn: Pre-built trackers (pricing, objections, risk signals): activation only, not editable, no credits.
features.on: Our built-ins are the AT&T rubric elements (including Objection handling) and the always-on competitor/topic intel. They are on by default rather than toggled on.

features.name: Example-based smart trackers
features.what: Trackers trained from example sentences rather than a question; English only. Basis: languages article and 'Create and manage example-based smart trackers' slug; method not read.
features.gn: The languages page lists example-based smart trackers under 'English only'. The training method itself is still undocumented.
features.on: No detector trained from example sentences.

features.name: Where tracker results appear
features.what: Call page Trackers panel with timestamps; Search filter grouped Keyword / Custom AI / By Gong; Team insights, streams, initiative boards, deals, scorecards, playbooks; exported to Salesforce by default for AI trackers.
features.gn: Call-page panel with timestamps; Search filter grouped Keyword/Custom AI/By Gong; insights, streams, deals, scorecards, playbooks. AI tracker results export to Salesforce by default.
features.on: Rubric results show on the pitch detail with play-at-timestamp chips and feed Pattern Interrupt; intel shows on the session panel. Nothing feeds a search filter or a CRM.

features.name: Trackers are per workspace
features.what: Set up in each workspace; keyword trackers can be copied to another workspace.
features.gn: Trackers are per workspace. Copying keyword trackers is CSV download, clear ID/Fingerprint columns, upload in the target workspace (Business admin).
features.on: The rubric is per company: one active rubric_config row per company, enforced by a unique index. There are no sub-workspaces and no copy.

features.name: Call topics on the timeline
features.what: Base English model (call setup, small talk, next steps, pricing, wrap-up) on by default; custom topics built with a Gong Revenue Architect; colour-coded under the player; main topic marked; click to jump. Reps can't create topics.
features.gn: English base model (Call Setup, Small Talk, Next Steps, Pricing, Wrap-up) on by default; custom topics via a Revenue Architect; colour-coded; main topic; click to jump; reps can't create topics.
features.on: Moments gives 3-5 key moments (opener, objection, breakdown, close) with real clock offsets, and intel gives topic names. There is no continuous topic lane under a player.

features.name: Search by topic share
features.what: Filter calls by topic and by how much of the call it occupied.
features.gn: You can filter by Call topic and by the percentage of the call the topic took up.
features.on: The sessions list cannot filter by topic or by topic share. Topics are stored as events, not as queryable columns.

modules.name: Search, library & streams
modules.summary: Our session history has basic filters (context, status, period) and a client/rep name text box. There is no transcript search, no score or topic filters, no saved searches, and no session export. We have no call library, folders or streams; the nearest things are the One Liners/Strategy Library of saved better lines and the generated coaching materials, and the only push alert is Pattern Interrupt's manager notification.
modules.vsum: Claims held. All four inferred slugs exist and support the inference, with one correction: global search does not list deals.

features.name: Call search with 100+ filters
features.what: Participants (hosted/attended/invited, email sender/recipient); account, title (operators), date, duration, direction; words/phrases with include/exclude; trackers; topics; scorecard overall/range/answers; comments and hashtags; shared; talk ratio, longest monologue, interactivity, patience; deal, stage, owner, imported CRM fields. AND/OR logic.
features.gn: The page says '100+ filters', and every listed filter matches. AND/OR logic is only referenced (it lives in 'Search for calls'); about 25 filters are actually named.
features.on: Server-side filters for context, status and period, plus a client-side text match on client/rep name. No transcript full-text search and no filters on score, talk metrics or topic.

features.name: Saved searches
features.what: Save and reuse a filter set. Basis: 'Save and reuse searches' slug; content not read.
features.gn: The article exists. Saved searches sit in a dropdown on the Search filter panel; they can't be shared and send no alerts (Gong points you to streams for that).
features.on: No saved filter sets. Searched for saved_search, savedSearch and bookmark; none found.

features.name: Download call data
features.what: Export search results. Basis: 'Download call data' slug.
features.gn: The article exists. The CSV (one row per call, optional CRM/tracker/topic/participant data) is emailed, not downloaded, and needs the 'Export reports to CSV' permission.
features.on: Only the KPI page exports a CSV, and it holds aggregate metrics. The session list cannot be exported.

features.name: Global search for anything
features.what: One search box across calls, accounts, deals, people. Basis: 'Search for anything in Gong' slug.
features.gn: The article exists. Top-bar search covers accounts, contacts/leads, calls, transcripts and comment hashtags. Deals are not mentioned.
features.on: /dashboard/search searches files, team chat and support messages, and Cmd+K jumps to pages. Neither one searches sales sessions or transcripts.

features.name: Your library and Company library
features.what: Private library (your folders, folders shared with you) and company library (visible to all with access; used for onboarding playlists, best practice, deal-stage references). Per workspace.
features.gn: Private Your library vs Company library (onboarding, best practice, deal-stage references); separate per workspace.
features.on: No call library. The One Liners/Strategy Library collects the better lines saved from each rep's reviews, and the coaching-materials library is AI-generated per skill. Neither curates calls.

features.name: Folders with nesting and notes
features.what: Manual containers; nested; the same call in many folders without duplication; optional note when saving; archiving a folder leaves calls searchable.
features.gn: Folders are manual, nestable, hold one call in many folders without copies, take an optional note; archived calls stay searchable.
features.on: No folders for sessions. Searched for library, playlist and folder in the sales-coach code and migrations.

features.name: Streams
features.what: Filter-driven collections (participants, accounts, keywords, trackers, deal stage) that add matching calls automatically; notify via Slack, Teams or email; private or company.
features.gn: Filter-driven auto-collections (participants, accounts, keywords, trackers, deal stage) with Slack/Teams/email notifications; private or company.
features.on: There are no user-defined streams. Pattern Interrupt pushes one fixed alert: a manager is notified when a rep crosses a repeated-miss threshold (3 of the last 10).

features.name: Share a folder
features.what: Owner shares a folder; it appears under 'Folders shared with you'; owner keeps ownership; unsharing removes it.
features.gn: Shared folders appear under 'Folders shared with you'; the owner keeps ownership; unsharing removes the folder from the list.
features.on: No folder sharing, because there are no folders. Sessions are visible to managers through company RLS, not through sharing.

features.name: Folder usage report
features.what: Downloadable report of who used a folder. Basis: 'Download a folder usage report' slug.
features.gn: The article exists. CSV of who listened to which call, when and for how long, plus a manager chain up to 10 levels. Business admin; Foundation plan.
features.on: We don't track who listened to which session recording.

modules.name: AI summaries, briefs, follow-ups & Gong Assistant
modules.summary: Our per-call AI layer is strong. Each sales call gets a factual summary, key moments, a pivot, a dissect, intel and a timestamped pitch score, and reps get a pre-knock 'Prep me' briefing; managers get a nightly team training brief. What we lack: admin-editable brief templates, contact/account briefs, follow-up email drafts, and a real assistant (Ask Coach is a single-turn, per-call question box with no saved history, no structured citations and no cross-call or file context).
modules.vsum: Claims held. The automated-briefs inference is right, but they are triggered by CRM events, not on a schedule. The 'Use deep mode' permission is on the permissions page, not the cited Assistant page.

features.name: Call highlights brief
features.what: Top of the call page: key moments, recap of main points, next steps.
features.gn: The call page says Highlights 'surfaces key moments, a recap with the main points covered, and next steps'. Its position at the top of the page isn't stated.
features.on: Each sales call gets a factual summary (discussed, objections, agreed, open), 3-5 timed key moments, a pivot, a dissect and intel, all generated together after the call.

features.name: Brief types as templates
features.what: A brief type has sections; each section is a question plus optional instructions and declared sources (calls/emails, CRM/Gong data, web). Gong ships defaults; admins create custom types (handoffs, deal progress).
features.gn: A brief type is a set of sections (question, optional instructions, sources: calls/emails, CRM/Gong, web). Gong ships defaults; admins create custom types (handoffs, deal progress).
features.on: Every summary engine runs a fixed prompt in code; admins can't define brief templates. The only admin-shaped config is the rubric.

features.name: Switch brief type on a call
features.what: Users switch brief types from the call page.
features.gn: AI Briefer: 'Users can switch to other brief types from the call page.'
features.on: There's no brief-type picker. The session page shows several fixed lenses side by side (summary, dissect, why, after-pitch, pitch score).

features.name: Contact, account and deal briefs
features.what: Contact: background, interests, challenges (meeting prep). Account/deal: conversations over a period + web + CRM; shown on Home, account console and deal boards (Briefs tab).
features.gn: Contact briefs: background, interests, challenges. Account/deal briefs cover a period plus web and CRM and show on Home, the account console and the deal board Briefs tab.
features.on: We have no contact, account or deal entity to brief on. Door-to-door sessions carry a client label only. The team training brief is team-scoped, not per account.

features.name: Automated briefs
features.what: Briefs generated on a schedule or trigger. Basis: 'Set up automated AI briefs' slug.
features.gn: The article exists. Triggers are CRM events on Account/Opportunity (created, field updated, date-relative), delivered by email to Gong users. Foundation plan.
features.on: A nightly cron pre-generates each company's team training brief for the Training tab. It is time-triggered, not event-triggered, and not emailed.

features.name: Meeting prep
features.what: AI-powered prep for upcoming meetings. Basis: 'Get ready for meetings with AI-powered meeting prep' slug.
features.gn: The article exists. Pre-meeting summary, ask-anything, participants, recent activity and an AI dry run, available from 15 min before the call. Needs prior activity.
features.on: Sales 'Prep me' gives a short pre-knock briefing plus prep Q&A. Meeting Coach has prep-up (goal, topics, docs). Neither draws on prior history with the same customer.

features.name: Follow-up email draft
features.what: Draft from transcript + meeting metadata; choose summary style; matches call language (regenerate in English); recording link only if external sharing allowed; copy out, or open in Engage composer (needs Engage).
features.gn: Drafted from transcript and metadata; summary style; call language with Regenerate-in-English; recording link only if external sharing is on; copy out, or Engage composer.
features.on: No follow-up email draft. A grep for 'follow-up email' and followUpEmail found nothing. It matters less for door knocks but would apply to phone/video reps.
