features.name: Gong Assistant chat
features.what: Chat panel opened from call page, search, account console, library or its own page; starting point sets initial context; infers timeframes, accounts, people from phrasing; uses only data the user can access; chats saved privately; follow-ups use history.
features.gn: Opens from the call page, Search, account console, library and its own page. Starting point sets context; it infers timeframes and people; uses only accessible data; chats private and persistent.
features.on: Ask Coach answers one free-form question about one session from its transcript. It is single-turn, keeps no history, isn't saved, and has no other entry points.

features.name: Answers cite transcript moments
features.what: On a call, the Assistant answers questions and cites matching transcript moments.
features.gn: The call page says the Assistant 'cites the exact moments in the transcript where it found the answer'.
features.on: Ask Coach is only told in its prompt to 'point to specific moments' and returns plain text, with no clickable citations. Pitch-score elements do have clickable timestamp chips.

features.name: Add calls, folders, streams, files as context
features.what: User picks calls, folders, streams or uploads files (playbooks, drafts, templates); files stay with that chat.
features.gn: Add calls, folders, streams or uploaded files (playbooks, drafts, templates); files stay with the chat.
features.on: Ask Coach can't take extra calls or files. File upload exists only in Meeting Coach prep docs (image/text/pdf), which feed the live meeting coach, not a chat.

features.name: Create documents and assets
features.what: Produce enablement docs, battlecards, FAQs, call scripts and scorecards; separate permissions for documents vs assets; revise in place.
features.gn: Enablement docs, battlecards, FAQs, call scripts, scorecards; 'Create documents' and 'Build assets' permissions; revise on the Assistant page.
features.on: The coaching-materials engine writes short skill drills from the team playbook, and practice scenarios are generated too. Neither is chat-driven, and there are no battlecards/FAQs or in-place revisions.

features.name: Deep mode
features.what: Longer, more detailed reports; gated by 'Use deep mode' permission.
features.gn: Deep mode for longer reports is confirmed on the Assistant page. The 'Use deep mode' permission is on the permissions page only, not the cited source.
features.on: No deep or multi-step research mode.

features.name: Ask questions across multiple calls
features.what: Ask one question over a set of calls. Basis: slug 'ask-questions-across-multiple-calls'.
features.gn: The article exists. Ask from Search (uses the current results), the Assistant page (+ calls/folders/streams) or the library. No call cap is stated.
features.on: Cross-call analysis exists but runs fixed questions, not free-form ones: why-patterns across a rep's last 60 sessions (4+ needed), and the team brief pooled across team dissects.

modules.name: Theme Spotter & market insights
modules.summary: The nearest match is the team training brief: it pools growth areas and strategy gaps across the team's dissects into 2-3 themes with a 'why', a drill and a focus line per rep, and refuses to run below 3 dissects. It cannot take a manager's question or filters, has no sub-themes, quotes or links back to calls, and can't turn a theme into a detector. There is no market/competitor trend view across the customer base, even though competitors are captured on every call.
modules.vsum: All Theme Spotter facts (6-hour runtime, 10,000-to-500 example, 20+3/60 seats max 30, 50k calls, reset on the 1st) were confirmed verbatim. The Market page inference holds.

features.name: Theme analysis
features.what: Input: a question + call filters. Output: themes with summaries, sub-themes, quotes and links to calls. Runs up to six hours.
features.gn: Question plus call filters in; themes with summaries, sub-themes, quotes and links to calls out. 'An analysis can take up to six hours.'
features.on: The team training brief produces themes, each with a 'why', from pooled team dissects. There's no question input, no filters, no sub-themes, and no quotes or links back to specific calls.

features.name: Runs only on tracker-flagged calls
features.what: Needs a published AI tracker for the question; only calls where it fired are analysed (10,000 filter matches may yield 500).
features.gn: Requires a published AI tracker for the question; uses only calls where it 'found something' (10,000 matches may yield 500).
features.on: Our pre-filter is a signal threshold instead of a tracker: no brief below 3 dissects, so the LLM never runs on thin data.

features.name: Monthly analysis quota
features.what: 20 per month + 3 per 60 seats, max 30; each up to 50,000 calls; resets on the 1st in company timezone.
features.gn: 20/month + 3 per 60 seats, max 30; up to 50,000 calls each; resets on the 1st in company timezone.
features.on: No monthly analysis quota. The brief is bounded by the nightly cron and a sequential per-company cap.

features.name: Turn a theme into a tracker
features.what: Users with tracker permission convert a theme into an AI tracker.
features.gn: Turning a theme into an AI tracker needs the Manage AI Tracker settings permission.
features.on: A theme can't be turned into an ongoing detector, because there are no user-defined trackers (see F11.2).

features.name: Shared list, permission-filtered calls
features.what: Analyses are listed for everyone with the page permission, but each viewer sees only calls they can access.
features.gn: Everyone with the AI Theme Spotter permission sees the shared list but 'only the calls they already have access to'.
features.on: There's one cached brief per company for managers. It has no call links, so per-viewer call filtering doesn't come up.

features.name: Market page
features.what: Insights > Market: trends across the customer base and their effect on deals. Basis: Enable marketing page and permission list name it; details not read.
features.gn: The marketing page says 'View trends across your customer base and learn how they affect your business, right down to specific deals'. The permissions page lists a Market page (Enable Essentials).
features.on: Competitors and topics are extracted per call and stored as events, but nothing adds them up into market or competitor trends or ties them to outcomes.

modules.name: Scorecards & AI Call Reviewer
modules.summary: Our engine already covers what Gong's AI Call Reviewer does: auto-scoring on close, a backfill drain, a computed score, a versioned rubric, logged per-item manager overrides with notification, evidence with timestamps, and a working rep dispute flow. What we lack is configurability: one hard-coded rubric with no question builder, ranges, editable weights, per-scorecard filters, visibility settings or N/A per item. The one serious defect is non-determinism (details under F15.15).
modules.vsum: All 19 OBSERVED claims were confirmed against the four cited Gong pages. The F15.20 gap claim is contradicted (Gong does show rationale and transcript evidence); the F15.21 gap holds.

features.name: Five question types
features.what: Range (rating scale), Yes/No, Single-select, Multi-select, Open-ended. Type can't change after publish.
features.gn: Source lists Range, Yes/No, Single-select, Multi-select, Open-ended; type can't change after publish.
features.on: One fixed AT&T Fiber rubric in code: 30 elements graded hit/partial/missed, 13 bonuses, 5 violations. No question builder; rubric_config table exists but nothing reads it.

features.name: Range scales
features.what: Min 0 or 1, max up to 50, default 0–10.
features.gn: Min 0 or 1, max up to 50, default 0-10 all stated.
features.on: No numeric range scale. Each element is a 3-level grade (hit=1, partial=0.5, missed=0) times its fixed points.

features.name: Weights summing to 100%
features.what: Only Range and Yes/No are weightable; weights must total 100%; 'Recalibrate to 100%' normalises.
features.gn: Only Range and Yes/No weightable; must total 100%; 'Recalibrate to 100%' button stated.
features.on: Weights are fixed point values per element. Sections sum to 100 (12/16/14/15/8/35), and a unit test checks that on every commit. No weight editor.

features.name: Calculated overall score
features.what: Yes=1, No=0; each Range answer normalised 0–1 by position between min and max; × weight; summed; scaled to the overall range (up to 0–100) and rounded. N/A answers are excluded and remaining weights rescaled; skipped weighted questions count as lowest value. Alternative: manually scored overall.
features.gn: Formula stated exactly: Yes=1/No=0, range normalised, weighted sum scaled and rounded; N/A excluded and reweighted; skipped = lowest; manual option.
features.on: Pure scorePitch(): base + min(bonus,30) - violations, floored at 0, on a 0-130 scale. The model grades, the code does the math, and the qualifying rule needs 40 base plus Discovery.

features.name: Mandatory questions and N/A
features.what: 'Make this question mandatory' prevents skip/N/A; otherwise reviewers can mark N/A.
features.gn: 'Make this question mandatory' prevents skip/N/A; otherwise N/A allowed.
features.on: One built-in N/A: Objection handling is skipped when no objection occurs, and the rest of Delivery is scaled from 27 to 35. There is no general N/A or mandatory flag per item.

features.name: Answer guide for the scorer
features.what: Rich-text instructions under each question so humans score consistently.
features.gn: Answer guide appears under the question; supports formatted text and links.
features.on: Each element has whatCounts text. It goes into the LLM prompt and shows in the rep-facing 'How points work' rubric sheet. It isn't a rich-text guide for human scorers.

features.name: Per-question AI mode
features.what: No AI; Get answer from AI (separate AI-facing question + 'what a correct answer looks like'; reviewer can keep or change); or Find answer with an AI tracker (shows snippets, no answer). Tools: Improve question, Test it on a real call. Not available for voicemail or transcripts under 100 words.
features.gn: No AI / Get answer from AI / AI tracker, Improve question, Test it, voicemail & <100-word floor all stated.
features.on: Every item is graded by AI; there is no per-item human-only or snippet-only mode. Calibration covers gamification dimensions, not this rubric. Minimum is 1 rep segment, so a 15s door rejection still gets scored.

features.name: Automatic review (AI Call Reviewer)
features.what: Every question must be 'Get answer from AI'; overall must be calculated. Scores new matching calls as they arrive; unanswerable questions are skipped; calls skipped if transcript too short or speaker data incomplete. Results labelled 'Scored by Gong AI'. Tech admin must enable it company-wide.
features.gn: Requirements (all AI questions, calculated overall, tech-admin enable), skips, and 'Scored by Gong AI' label confirmed across both URLs.
features.on: Sales calls are auto-scored on session close (skipIfScored:true), and a cron/drain handles the rest. Gaps: the model and prompt version aren't stored (only rubric_version), and there is no admin on/off switch.

features.name: Call selection filters for auto-review
features.what: A call is scored only if it matches all filters: participants (hosted/attended/invited), account, words or phrases, trackers, title.
features.gn: Participants (hosted/attended/invited), account, words/phrases, trackers, title; must match all.
features.on: The only filter is isSalesCall(): huddles and meetings are refused. With one rubric for every sales call, there's no per-scorecard filter by channel (door/phone/video), keyword or account.

features.name: Who gets scored
features.what: Default: call host only. Or selected teams/people, each getting their own scorecard, max three per call from the selected team.
features.gn: Host by default; or teams/people, each scored, max three per call from selected team.
features.on: Scores exactly one person: the session's agent (rep_id = session.agentId). That fits one-rep door/phone pitches. Multi-rep calls aren't supported.

features.name: Apply to past 90 days
features.what: Backfill matching calls from the last 90 days in the background; email on completion (not a guarantee every call was scored).
features.gn: 90-day background backfill, email on completion, no guarantee all scored, published only.
features.on: Backfill route: GET shows the unscored count for free, POST scores batches of 8 and reports refusals by reason. 'Generate missing' button on Coach Assessment. No 90-day limit and no completion email.

features.name: Score visibility
features.what: Per scorecard: Everyone (default, 'Public'); Scored member + their managers; Manager and above; Scorer only (for AI, nobody else sees it). Restricted results show a badge. Manual scorers may override visibility per call; AI results always use the scorecard setting.
features.gn: Four options (Everyone default/Public, scored+managers, Manager, Scorer); Restricted badge; manual per-call override; AI fixed.
features.on: Fixed visibility in RLS: the rep sees their own scores and company managers see all. It can't be configured, and there's no Restricted badge. Peers see only leaderboard totals.

features.name: Notify the scored person
features.what: Optional 'Send notifications to people who are scored'; only reaches people allowed to see the result.
features.gn: 'Send notifications to people who are scored'; only reaches those allowed to see the result.
features.on: The rep is notified when a manager corrects a score (upsert, re-marked unread) and when a manager sends a comment. No notification when the first AI score lands, because the rep triggers it at session close.

features.name: Override AI scores
features.what: Only users with 'Override score' can edit or delete an AI result. No accept or dispute step is documented.
features.gn: 'Override score' permission can edit or delete AI results; no accept/dispute step mentioned.
features.on: More than Gong: managers override each element, bonus or violation. A reason is required (schema, CHECK, RPC), logged in pitch_score_overrides, the score is recomputed through scorePitch, and the rep is notified.

features.name: AI scores are not deterministic
features.what: Gong states its AI can give different answers to the same question on the same call.
features.gn: Quote: 'Gong AI can sometimes give different answers to the same question, even on the same call.' Echoed in gong-ai-for-scoring.
features.on: Auto paths score once (skipIfScored). But the score API has no manager gate and passes skipIfScored:false, so a rep (session owner) can re-roll via API. Re-score replaces the score, wiping evidence and override effects.

features.name: Learning resources on low scores
features.what: Attach content that appears on the call page when a call scores low.
features.gn: 'Include resources' toggle; content appears on call page when call scores low.
features.on: No static resource links. Instead: practice-scenario-from-pitch rebuilds a roleplay from the rep's actual pitch, focused on their weakest area, and Pattern Interrupt lets managers assign drills.

features.name: Destructive edits warning
features.what: Removing a question with results permanently deletes its answers; deleting the overall score deletes stored overall answers, and re-adding doesn't restore them.
features.gn: Removing a question deletes its answers permanently; deleting overall deletes stored overall answers, re-adding doesn't restore.
features.on: Rubric is versioned. pitch_scores.rubric_version is a foreign key to rubric_config, and a rubric change must be a new version, so old scores stay explainable. But re-scoring the same pitch deletes its old evidence rows.

features.name: Scorecard name filter in search
features.what: Find calls scored by a specific scorecard via Conversations Search.
features.gn: 'Scorecard name' filter in Conversations Search stated.
features.on: Not needed while there's one rubric. The recordings list shows score, band and 'Not counted', but there's no filter by rubric version or score.

features.name: Scorecards via API
features.what: List scorecard definitions; list answered scorecards per user.
features.gn: llms.txt lists 'Retrieve scorecards details (/v2/settings/scorecards)' and 'Retrieve answered scorecards ... (/v2/stats/activity/scorecards)'.
features.on: Internal app routes only (rubric, breakdown, leaderboard, report-card). There's no public or partner API, and the generic CSV export doesn't include pitch scores.

features.name: Evidence quotes per AI answer
features.what: Gong's articles do not document evidence or quotes behind AI answers. Proposal: every AI answer stores the transcript timestamps it relied on, shown as 'jump to moment' links, so a rep can see why they got the points.
features.gn: Absence fails: help.gong.io/docs/answer-scorecard-questions-with-ai-call-reviewer says 'Click AI answer to read the AI's rationale and the transcript evidence it used.' No timestamps mentioned.
features.on: Already built: every element stores a timestamp and evidence quote. Pitch Detail shows them with jump-to-moment play, and rejected bonus confidences are kept. Reps see the evidence on their own pitches.

features.name: Rep dispute of an AI score
features.what: Gong documents no accept or dispute flow; only override-permission holders can change AI results. When scores become points on a leaderboard, reps will contest them. Proposal: 'request review' on an AI result that lands in the manager's coaching inbox.
features.gn: Absence holds: none of review/answer/gong-ai-for-scoring pages, nor web search, describe a rep dispute flow.
features.on: Built: reps dispute a score or one item, with a timestamp (an event, not a score change); managers answer from a queue. Gaps: filing a dispute sends the manager no notification, and answering doesn't notify the rep.

modules.name: Feedback, coaching inbox & coaching metrics
modules.summary: We have pieces of a coaching inbox on Coach Assessment: dispute queue, rude-flag review, timestamped manager comments sent to reps, and a pattern 'Mark as coached' whose follow-up checks whether the rep improved, which is stronger than Gong's activity counts. We lack the manager-measurement layer: no rep 'request feedback', no rules for what counts as feedback, no listen tracking, no per-manager coaching metrics or export. Sales Coach also has no direct-report hierarchy to hang an inbox on.
modules.vsum: All 12 claims confirmed against the five cited Gong pages, including that AI and automatic scorecards don't count as feedback; F16.12's guides were read and are guide articles, not product features.

features.name: Feedback request
features.what: A rep requests feedback from the call's Feedback tab (manager preselected, anyone selectable) with a message; lands in the recipient's coaching inbox. Also counts: tagging the direct manager in a comment, or sharing an attended call with the direct manager.
features.gn: Feedback tab > Request feedback, manager preselected, anyone selectable, message, lands in coaching inbox; tag/share variants confirmed.
features.on: The only rep-to-manager request is a score dispute, which reaches the manager queue. No general 'request feedback' and no way to tag a manager. No per-rep manager link, so alerts go to all managers.

features.name: Precise 'feedback given' rules
features.what: Counts: manager comment where the rep is the only team member on the call; on multi-member calls only if the rep requested or the comment is private; reply to a rep's tag; scorecard visible to everyone/specific people/rep+manager; 'Mark it'. Doesn't count: scoring your own call, listening/attending, multi-tag comments, email feedback, AI scorecards.
features.gn: All rules confirmed incl. 'Automatic (AI) scorecards... tracked separately' not counted; Scorer/Only-me scorecards excluded.
features.on: Nothing classifies or counts manager feedback. The pieces exist as rows (recording_comments.sent_to_rep, pitch_score_overrides, dispute answers, pattern 'coached' events), but no rule engine counts them per manager.

features.name: Mark feedback as given (offline coaching)
features.what: Log a 1:1 or ride-along coaching that happened outside the product: call > Feedback > Mark it.
features.gn: 'Mark it' on Feedback tab logs offline coaching (1:1/in-person); counts in Coaching metrics.
features.on: Managers 'Mark as coached' on a Pattern (a rubric weakness), not on a pitch. It's manager-only, and the pattern then tracks whether the miss rate improves (improving/stalled): coaching judged by outcome, not activity.

features.name: Request closure
features.what: A request closes when the manager comments, replies to the tag, scores, or marks feedback given.
features.gn: Closes on manager comment, reply to tag, score, or mark given; inbox count updates daily (up to 24h).
features.on: A dispute is open until a manager answer event follows it (worked out from the event history). A comment or override on that pitch doesn't close it, and only disputes have open/closed state.

features.name: Coaching inbox
features.what: One row per direct report, sorted by feedback given; columns Coaching activity, Last attended/listened, Last feedback (dash = none in 30 days = overdue), Open requests (last 30 days, unanswered), Recorded calls (feedback-requested first). Refreshes daily.
features.gn: Columns, 30-day windows, dash meaning, feedback-requested-first, daily refresh all stated; sort direction not specified.
features.on: Coach Assessment has a Dispute queue, Rude-flag review queue, 'Needs your attention' (prize eligibility, unscored backlog) and a Reps table. Missing per rep: last feedback, last listened, 30-day overdue, open requests.

features.name: Inbox actions and filters
features.what: GO TO CALL; filter recorded calls (no feedback, interaction alerts); comment, score, reply, mark given; switch to another manager's team; coaching selector: only theirs / only yours / both.
features.gn: GO TO CALL, filters (no feedback, interaction alerts), comment/score/reply/mark, manager dropdown, Only theirs/Only yours/Both.
features.on: Managers can comment at a timestamp (send to rep or save as draft), override, answer disputes, and confirm/remove rude flags. No 'no-feedback-yet' filter, no switching to another manager's team, no theirs/yours selector.

features.name: Inbox scope limits
features.what: Only external calls linked to an account or opportunity where the rep hosted appear; rep must be a direct report.
features.gn: Only external calls tied to account/opportunity, rep-hosted, direct report.
features.on: No CRM or account requirement: every sales session is in scope (good for door pitches). But there's also no direct-report hierarchy; the manager is any is_sales_coach_manager in the company.

features.name: Coaching metrics per manager
features.what: Columns: Calls listened (once per call, live or recording), Calls attended, Calls with feedback, Calls with comments, Calls with scorecards, Manually gave feedback. Filters: team, manager level (all/direct/level-1), period, call type. Arrows vs previous period; sortable; drill to calls.
features.gn: Six columns, team/manager-level/period/call-type filters, arrows, sort, drill-down all stated.
features.on: No per-manager coaching-activity table. Team/KPI/analytics pages measure reps (pitch score, doors, close %, coaching grade), not managers.

features.name: Activity counted when coaching happened
features.what: Listening three months after recording counts in the month it was listened to.
features.gn: 'a call listened to three months after recording counts in the period it was listened to.'
features.on: There's no manager metric to time. Pattern coachedAt does use the coaching-event time, so the rule is easy to keep if metrics are built.

features.name: Listening tracking
features.what: The product records when a manager listens to a rep's call (needed for 'Calls listened'). Basis: metric exists; the threshold for 'listened' is not documented.
features.gn: 'Calls listened' counted once per call, live or recording; page states no minimum listening duration (threshold undocumented, as artifact says).
features.on: Manager playback isn't tracked at all: no listen/progress events on recording playback.

features.name: Coaching export and monthly email
features.what: Export per-manager summary or per-call rows; subscribe to a monthly coaching report (requires CRM integration).
features.gn: Per-manager or per-call export; monthly subscription via Manage Subscriptions; CRM integration required.
features.on: No coaching export or monthly digest. The generic export covers tasks, problems, resolutions, signals, events and dialogues only.

features.name: Coaching routines
features.what: Gong publishes guided routines: a self-coaching routine for reps and a weekly routine for managers. Basis: article slugs; content not read.
features.gn: Both slugs exist; content read: rep 6-step self-coaching routine; manager 5-step weekly routine (guide articles, not product features).
features.on: No published coaching routines. The nearest thing is the team training brief ('What the team needs to work on'), generated weekly.

modules.name: AI Trainer, role-play & lessons
modules.summary: Gong's AI Trainer is a real, well-documented voice role-play product: trainings made of lessons and practice modules, scenarios built from real calls, and scoring with the same scorecard used on live calls. Ours is a text-only role-play with 4 fixed personas plus AI-generated scenarios (from a skill focus or a real recorded pitch), scored 0-100 on one focus skill. We have no lesson builder, assignments, due dates or submissions, and Bootcamp is an empty placeholder.
modules.vsum: All 14 claims confirmed on Gong's help pages; Gemini Live is named on the v1 how-to page as the language/voice provider.

features.name: Training = ordered lessons and practices
features.what: Name, short description, optional overview; add Lesson or Practice modules; reorder; autosave.
features.gn: Name, short description, optional overview; lesson + practice modules in any order; modules autosave, then 'Save training'.
features.on: No training/module builder or tables. Bootcamp lists one hardcoded area whose page says 'Materials coming'. The Training tab shows LLM-derived growth areas, not authored trainings.

features.name: Lesson content blocks
features.what: Rich text; a Gong call or snippet (optional Mandatory watch: no skip, no speed-up); external Loom, YouTube or Google Slides (not tracked).
features.gn: Rich text, Gong call/snippet by URL with Mandatory watch (no skip, no faster playback), Loom/YouTube/Google Slides embeds that are not tracked.
features.on: No lesson content blocks. The nearest thing is coachingMaterial/TeamTrainingBriefPanel (an LLM-written brief), not authored lessons with clips.

features.name: Scenario from real calls
features.what: Description (goal, context, objections), optional call/snippet links that set the customer voice, more information. AI then prefills: contact persona (title, responsibilities, motivations, style; editable name, avatar, voice), customer company, meeting objective, scenario, relationship background, about our company, difficulty (Easy/Intermediate/Advanced), length 5–30 min, background for trainee.
features.gn: All listed fields present: persona title/responsibilities/motivations/style, name/avatar/voice, company, objective, relationship, about us, Easy/Intermediate/Advanced, 5-30 min.
features.on: Scenario = title + persona + situation. It is AI-generated from a focus skill, or rebuilt from a real recorded pitch transcript (strong analogue). No difficulty, length, company or avatar/voice fields, and scenarios are not stored or reusable.

features.name: Test the scenario
features.what: Admin tests up to 9 minutes with the persona; edits update live; 'Redo scenario inputs' resets.
features.gn: Test session allows 'up to 9 minutes'; 'Redo scenario inputs' resets to the original inputs.
features.on: There is no admin authoring step, so there is no admin test mode. Reps can regenerate a scenario before practising.

features.name: Voice role-play
features.what: Trainee clicks Start, then Start recording; talks to an AI customer that responds dynamically; company/contact background in a side panel; any supported language; quiet place recommended. Gong uses Gemini Live for voice.
features.gn: Start, then Start recording; dynamic AI customer; background in a side panel; any supported language; quiet place required. v1 how-to page: 'Language support is provided through Google's Gemini Live API'.
features.on: Text-only, turn-based LLM prospect (in-person or video context). Voice was deferred ('text-first'). The conversation is held client-side in sessionStorage. Nothing is persisted except the score event. Works on mobile web.

features.name: Scored by the live-call scorecard
features.what: Practice is scored by an automatic-review scorecard through AI Call Reviewer, so practice and live feedback use the same criteria; overall score and per-element breakdown; private to the trainee.
features.gn: ai-trainer page: evaluated by AI Call Reviewer with 'the same scorecards applied to live calls'; overall score plus breakdown; feedback visible only to the trainee.
features.on: Practice is NOT scored by the live rubric (Pitch Score / after-pitch dimensions). A separate LLM review gives a 0-100 score on one focus skill, and only when launched from a focus. A plain roleplay gets an unscored review.

features.name: Pass threshold and unlimited retries
features.what: Optional minimum score to pass a module; 'Go again' unlimited before submit; resubmit later (latest score shown); unsubmitted progress kept 90 days.
features.gn: Optional minimum score gates Next/submit; repeat as often as you want; resubmit (latest score shown); unsubmitted progress kept 90 days.
features.on: 'Practice again' gives unlimited retries, and every scored attempt is logged. There is no pass threshold, submit step or 'latest score' assignment view.

features.name: AI Coach Q&A after each session
features.what: 'Let's talk' opens a chat to ask follow-ups (how to handle an objection differently, what to focus on).
features.gn: 'Let's talk' opens a conversation with the AI coach for follow-up questions.
features.on: The roleplay ends at a static review card (what worked / to improve / correct line). There is no follow-up chat tied to the attempt.

features.name: Practice calls marked internal
features.what: Practice calls are internal: smart trackers don't run and conversation stats aren't affected; private option limits to trainee, manager chain and notified people.
features.gn: AI Trainer calls are marked internal: no smart trackers, no effect on conversation stats; private checkbox limits access (private calls still appear in Search/Stats).
features.on: Practice is isolated by design. It is not persisted as a session, earns no gamification points and doesn't touch metrics. Only an append-only coach.practice_scored event feeds a growth trend, deliberately unranked.

features.name: Assignments with due dates
features.what: Assign to a team or person with a due date; copy link (people join the list on submit); average score per module; click a score to hear the attempt; bulk change due dates; download CSV.
features.gn: Assign to teams/individuals with due date; Copy link (added on submit); module average score; click score to listen; bulk due-date changes; Download CSV.
features.on: No assignments or due dates. Managers see each rep's LLM-derived growth areas and practice trend on the Training tab, but cannot assign practice.

features.name: Submission notifies manager
features.what: Submit notifies direct manager by default plus chosen people/teams.
features.gn: Direct manager notified by default, plus people/teams you add; each resubmission emails the manager again.
features.on: Practice sends no notification. manager_notifications only allows 'strong_session' and 'deal_closed'. The manager sees practice activity only by visiting the Training tab.

features.name: Dry Run for an upcoming meeting
features.what: Practice a specific upcoming meeting; persona and account context replicated automatically, no setup.
features.gn: Marketing page: Gong 'automatically replicates the real customer persona and account context' before a meeting. No help-centre article (no 'dry run' slug in llms.txt).
features.on: There is no forward-looking dry run, which suits door-to-door with no scheduled meetings. The backward version exists: 'role-play from a recorded pitch' rebuilds that exact customer so the rep can replay it.

features.name: Lessons as learning programmes
features.what: Structured role-specific programmes mixing micro-learnings, practice and assessments.
features.gn: Marketing page: 'flexible course formats that include micro-learnings, practice, and assessments.'
features.on: Bootcamp was built as the hub for programmes, but its content model is explicitly undecided and it has no material yet.

features.name: Enable seat required
features.what: AI Trainer is in Enable, not Enable Essentials; web only, not mobile.
features.gn: introduction-to-coaching: Enable = Essentials 'plus AI Trainer'; 'Enable features are available in the Gong web app only.'
features.on: Our roleplay is a page inside the responsive app, with no seat gating, so phone reps can use it. Text input avoids the 'quiet place' requirement but loses voice realism.

modules.name: Initiatives & adoption tracking
modules.summary: Gong's Initiative boards measure what share of calls (or deals) mention a tracker, per team and rep over time, coloured against a high or low adoption goal. We have nothing tracker-based. The closest analogue is Pattern Interrupt, which tracks per-rep repeated misses of rubric elements over time, and a cue-to-outcome correlation in the KPI layer.
modules.vsum: The help article confirms every mechanic. The outcome-correlation claim appears only on the marketing page, as the artifact says.

features.name: Initiative board
features.what: Board with several trackers (one line each), board filters (team, period) and per-tracker filters (e.g. discovery calls only); call-based or deal-based.
features.gn: Insights > Initiatives; multiple trackers per board; board and per-tracker filters; deal-based or call-based; periods 90d/30d/month/week/custom.
features.on: No initiative boards and no keyword trackers. Pattern Interrupt watches rubric-element misses per rep, not chosen phrases. It is not configurable as 'did reps adopt the new line'.

features.name: Adoption calculation
features.what: Call-based: % of the team's owned calls mentioning the tracker. Deal-based: % of deals-with-calls where it was mentioned.
features.gn: Call-based: calls mentioning the tracker ÷ total calls. Deal-based: deals with a mention ÷ deals with calls.
features.on: No mention-rate calculation. Pattern detection counts misses within a window of applicable pitches (MISS_THRESHOLD/WINDOW). That is a different question (a repeated miss, not adoption %).

features.name: High- and low-adoption goals
features.what: Green when a high goal is met (used often) or a low goal is met (retired messaging rarely used); red otherwise.
features.gn: Each tracker has a high or low goal with a % threshold; green when met, red when not; low goal = term should rarely appear.
features.on: No goal or threshold per message. A 'low-adoption' (retired line) concept does not exist.

features.name: Adoption over time and by team
features.what: Line graph per tracker by day/week/month; grid of teams and individuals with team average row; click a manager to drill; click a person for calls/deals with snippets.
features.gn: Line per tracker by day/week/month (week/month only if period >60 days); team/individual grid with team average row; manager drill-down; side panel with snippets.
features.on: The Rep progress board shows per-rep patterns over time with coaching markers and a needs-attention sort, but no team-by-element adoption grid or % trend line.

features.name: Adoption vs outcomes
features.what: Marketing claims initiative tracking correlates behaviour change with win rate, deal size and ramp time; the help article does not describe it.
features.gn: Marketing page ties initiative tracking to 'win rates, deal size, and ramp time'; the help article does not mention it.
features.on: Not tied to initiatives, but the KPI layer computes a cue-to-outcome correlation (acted-cue rate vs WON, gated by minimum sessions). The door-log rollup asks the LLM to correlate behaviour with NO outcomes.

modules.name: Gamification (absent in Gong)
modules.summary: The claim mostly holds: Gong's help centre has no points, badges, streaks or contests, and these are sold by third parties (Spinify, Ambition, Kixie) on top of Gong. One exception: Engage Analytics marks the top performer per activity metric with a green crown, a light ranking. We have all four pieces built (points ledger, two scoreboards, 5 milestone badges, manager alerts, AI-derived day target), with one drift from the recorded decision: a weekly email digest exists alongside the in-app alerts.
modules.vsum: llms.txt has no leaderboard/points/badge/streak/contest slugs and the web searches found only third-party tools. The 'ranks nothing' wording is slightly overstated because of Engage's top-performer crowns.

features.name: Points per session
features.what: Gong scores calls (F15.4) but converts nothing into points. Your system awards points per session based on how it was handled, regardless of sale.
features.source: Absence across https://help.gong.io/llms.txt index (no points/leaderboard articles)
features.gn: No points/badges in llms.txt, product pages or the coaching intro. G2 lists a generic 'Leaderboard' category and Gong community threads ask how to gamify; points come from Spinify-type add-ons.
features.on: Points reuse the after-pitch dimension scores (mean×10, 0-100) and are banked once per session in an append-only ledger with a unique index. This answers the open M19 decision: points are frozen at first score.

features.name: Scoreboard
features.what: Gong ranks nothing publicly between reps; Team stats are tables for managers. Your system ranks agents on closed deals and points.
features.gn: Team stats has no ranking (rows/team totals only). But Engage Analytics: 'A green crown next to a number indicates the highest number of activities' (top performers).
features.on: Scoreboard page has two named boards: Pitch Score (the competition board) and Activity points. The leaderboard function orders by total points (deals shown, not the primary sort), with competition ranking (ties share a place).

features.name: Manager alert on strong session or close
features.what: Gong's nearest analogues are scorecard notifications (F15.13), streams with alerts (F12.7) and agents (M27), none built for praise. Your system alerts managers in-app when a session crosses the points threshold, and especially on a closed deal.
features.gn: No praise/alert-on-success feature found in docs or searches. Nearest analogues remain scorecard notifications and streams. control-scorecard-visibility was not fetched separately.
features.on: In-app manager_notifications with exactly 'strong_session' and 'deal_closed', idempotent, fanned out to company admins. Drift: weeklyDigest also EMAILS managers 'top performers', which conflicts with the 'in-app only' decision.

features.name: AI-derived daily door target
features.what: Gong has targets (M22) set by admins, not computed per rep from their own ratios. Your Home screen derives how many doors a rep must knock from their close ratio.
features.source: Absence: https://help.gong.io/llms.txt (targets are uploaded/managed, see manage-your-targets)
features.gn: llms.txt only has admin-managed/uploaded target slugs (create-and-manage-targets, manage-your-targets, troubleshoot-target-file-uploads). Their bodies were not read.
features.on: deriveDailySalesGoal sets the goal from the rep's own sales, or their activity when they have no sales. calculateDayTarget works it back through the 30-day close and contact ratios to doors/presentations/sold, with a starter until the rep qualifies.

modules.name: Deals & pipeline intelligence
modules.summary: Gong's deal boards are CRM opportunities with conversation data layered on: warnings, methodology playbooks, a daily win-likelihood score, and win/loss and rep-driver analytics. We have no deal or pipeline object. A sale is an outcome on one session (sold/no_sale/follow_up plus an optional deal_value), and a few deal-like KPIs are computed from that.
modules.vsum: Fetched all 6 cited help pages plus 3 slug pages: 13 of 14 features confirmed. Small differences: win/loss shows up to 20 won AND 20 lost deals, and the score sits in the drill-down rather than as a board column.

features.name: Deal boards: filters, tabs, columns
features.what: Filters segment by CRM fields; tabs group deals (e.g. forecast category, size) with roll-ups; columns show CRM fields, activity, warnings, playbook, smart trackers, AI-suggested updates, score. Conditional filters refine tabs and filters.
features.gn: Filters, tabs with roll-ups, CRM/playbook/activity/smart-tracker columns and conditional filters confirmed. Score is in the drill-down (Forecast seats only), not listed as a column.
features.on: No deal or opportunity entity and no board. The only CRM in the app is the vendor back office for ELOSTATE's own customer companies, not reps' prospects.

features.name: Inline CRM editing
features.what: Edit CRM fields in a cell or in the deal panel's Update CRM section (includes non-column fields); writes back to CRM.
features.gn: Edit in a column cell or in the deal panel's 'Update CRM' section, which holds fields that are not columns.
features.on: No CRM integration and no write-back. The only HubSpot/Salesforce mentions are placeholder copy on the marketing demo page.

features.name: Deal panel
features.what: Tabs: Score (signals, Forecast seats only), Briefs, Warnings with mitigations, Contacts, Deal activity timeline, Playbook, Update CRM.
features.gn: Drill-down tabs confirmed: Score (Forecast seats only), Briefs, Warnings with mitigation suggestions, Contacts, Deal activity timeline, Playbook, Update CRM.
features.on: No deal panel. The closest thing is the single-session detail page (/dashboard/sales-coach/[id]), which covers one conversation, not a multi-touch deal.

features.name: AI-suggested deal updates
features.what: A text CRM field like Next steps can be filled with suggestions from this and last week's conversations.
features.gn: One text-only CRM column (e.g. Next steps) can take AI-suggested updates drawn from this week's and last week's conversations.
features.on: No AI write-back to a deal field. The AI writes coaching reviews and after-pitch feedback, not CRM next-step text.

features.name: Deal warnings (8 types)
features.what: No activity (X days; typical 7/14/7), Ghosted (no prospect participation X days; 4/7/4), Overdue (close date passed), Not enough contacts (1–5 contacts for X days), No power (no Director/VP/C-level active within X days of close; fires when ≥75% of verified titles are below rank, from last 90 days), Pricing not mentioned (X days before close), Red flag email (English only; clears on reply or call), Stalled in stage (per-stage thresholds). Configured per board; calendar days.
features.gn: All 8 warnings confirmed with the stated typical thresholds (7/14/7, 4/7/4), the fixed 75%-of-titles rule over 90 days for No power, and calendar days.
features.on: No deal-risk warnings. Pattern Interrupt flags a rep's recurring pitch misses (with 'stalled' after 7 days), which is a skill pattern, not deal risk.

features.name: Methodology playbooks
features.what: Pre-built MEDDICC, BANT, SPIN, Challenger, SPICED, Solution Selling, Sandler; or custom. Each element is a letter on the board.
features.gn: Pre-built MEDDICC, BANT, SPIN, Challenger, SPICED, Solution Selling and Sandler, plus custom playbooks; each element shows as a letter on the board.
features.on: No sales-methodology playbooks (no MEDDIC/BANT anywhere). Our analogue is a versioned, company-specific pitch-scoring rubric (AT&T Fiber) scored per pitch, not per deal.

features.name: AI Deal Reviewer suggested notes
features.what: Each element mapped to an AI source (Gong playbook trackers, custom AI tracker, keyword tracker); AI finds conversation evidence and suggests a note; AE updates; AE or manager validates. Status colours: white (nothing), white+star (AI found evidence), light blue (manual note), dark blue (validated).
features.gn: Each element's AI source can be a playbook, custom AI or keyword tracker; AI suggests notes; AE updates; AE or manager validates; all 4 colour states confirmed.
features.on: The AI grades each rubric element from the transcript with cited evidence, and managers can override a score. It works per pitch, not as deal-element notes.

features.name: Playbook two-way CRM sync
features.what: Each element's status and note push to two fields on the CRM opportunity; changes sync both ways.
features.gn: Status and note push as two fields on the CRM opportunity, with two-way sync.
features.on: No CRM sync of any kind.

features.name: Deal likelihood score
features.what: Base model pre-trained across customers + tuned on your last two years of closed deals; rescored daily. ~50% conversation signals (legal, pricing, red flags, competitors, warnings, interaction stats), 50% activity/contacts/progression/history. Bands: Low 0–35, Fair 36–74, High 75–100. Claimed ~21% more precise than reps by week 4.
features.gn: Cross-customer base model tuned on 2 years of your closed deals; rescored daily; 50% conversation signals; bands 0-35/36-74/75-100; 21% claim confirmed. No minimum deal count stated.
features.on: No predictive win-likelihood model. The KPIs are descriptive and gated by sample size.

features.name: Win/loss analytics
features.what: Win rate = won/(won+lost); needs ≥100 qualifying closed deals. Compares by contact count, power in deal, duration, size, number of calls, competitor mentions (top 3 / other / none), and any tracker mentioned vs not. Click a bar for up to 20 deals; 'See the math' CSV includes excluded deals and why.
features.gn: Formula, the ≥100-closed-deal minimum, all dimensions and the 'See the math' CSV confirmed. Clicking a bar shows up to 20 won AND up to 20 lost deals, not 20 in total.
features.on: We compute close rate (won÷resolved) and a win/loss ratio, plus a cue-to-outcome correlation (a rough 'tracker vs win'). No breakdown by contact count, deal size, competitors or tracker.

features.name: Deal drivers
features.what: Per rep: open deals in period and % with each warning on at least one day; top three per column highlighted; >3 reps highlighted = team training need; now / 30 / 90 days.
features.gn: Per rep: % of open deals with each warning on ≥1 day; top 3 per column in yellow; >3 reps with a high % suggests team-wide training; Now/30/90 days.
features.on: Pattern Interrupt does the same per-rep-to-team-training move for pitch-skill misses: a team-wide banner when 3+ reps share an open pattern. It does not cover deal risks.

features.name: Opportunity teams and splits
features.what: Deals with multiple owners and revenue splits on boards. Basis: slugs 'work-with-opportunity-teams', 'apply-opportunity-splits-to-your-deal-board'.
features.gn: Help pages confirm opportunity teams (boards show deals where the person isn't the primary owner) and splits (share of the amount on the board, Salesforce only).
features.on: Each session or sale has a single rep. No co-owners and no revenue splits.

features.name: Board recipes
features.what: Documented board recipes: deals needing attention, renewals, swing deals, next-quarter pipe. Basis: recipe slugs.
features.gn: llms.txt lists recipes for needs-attention, renewals, swing deals and next-quarter pipe, and the needs-attention recipe page is a deal-board walkthrough for managers.
features.on: No deal boards, so no board templates.

features.name: Single-visit sale record
features.what: Gong's deal model assumes an opportunity spanning many interactions in a CRM. A door sale often opens and closes in one session. Proposal: a lightweight 'sale' attached to the session (amount, product, status) instead of a CRM opportunity, so 'deals closed' on the scoreboard doesn't need a CRM.
features.gn: A web search found no documented way to put a non-CRM or single-visit sale on a Gong board. Boards depend on synced CRM opportunities, which supports the gap claim.
features.on: Already largely built: coaching_sessions.outcome (sold/no_sale/follow_up…) plus deal_value, set via the outcome API, and door_knocks.outcome='sold'. Missing: product, closed_at, and a separate sales table.

modules.name: Accounts
modules.summary: Gong account boards list CRM accounts with Gong-computed activity levels, and the account console gives one account's full timeline. We have no account object for reps' customers. The closest pieces are the free-text client_label used as a prospect key, and a vendor-only CRM for ELOSTATE's own customer companies.
modules.vsum: Fetched both cited pages: all 5 observed features confirmed. The gap option was checked by web search, which found no address-level records in Gong.

features.name: Account boards
features.what: Grid of accounts; up to eight tabs from saved filters; columns from CRM (ARR, renewal date, health) or Gong (activity over time, activity level); default brief type per board.

modules.name: Engage flows & rulesets
modules.summary: Gong Engage is an email/call/LinkedIn sequencer: flows of timed steps, each governed by one ruleset that handles replies, bounces and CRM changes. We have no outbound sequencing at all. 'Cadence' and 'sequence' appear in the code only in unrelated senses, and the closest door feature is the go_back outcome with no automated follow-up.
modules.vsum: Fetched all 5 cited pages plus the API and migration pages: 9 of 9 confirmed, including the Nudge/Follow-up AI drafts and the Nov 2026 AI flow builder.

features.name: Flow step types
features.what: Manual email (waits on to-do; templates, placeholders, AI 'Nudge'/'Follow-up' drafts); Auto email (falls back to manual if placeholder missing, thread lost or mailbox disconnected); Call (Gong Dialer, recorded, script); LinkedIn connect (needs Sales Navigator Advanced Plus; can't log to CRM); LinkedIn message; Task.
features.gn: All 6 step types confirmed, incl. AI 'Nudge'/'Follow-up' drafts, auto-to-manual fallback, Gong or integrated dialer, and LinkedIn connect (Sales Navigator plus Advanced Plus, not loggable to CRM).
features.on: No flows or sequences. A grep for sequence/cadence/drip/outreach finds only unrelated uses (cron cadence, build sequence).

features.name: Step timing
features.what: First step delays from flow start, later from previous step; hours or business days; preferred morning (9–12) or afternoon (12–6) recipient time; auto emails send in recipient's local time (fallback sender's); first auto email 'as soon as possible' (business day) or any day.
features.gn: Delay from flow start, then from the previous step; hours or business days; recipient 9-12 or 12-6 slots (business days only); auto emails in recipient local time; first auto email ASAP.
features.on: No step scheduler.

features.name: Threading and recipients
features.what: Later email steps reply in thread or start new; preset To/CC/BCC; 'My manager' placeholder in manual emails.
features.gn: Later steps can reply in thread or start a new thread; preset To/CC/BCC; 'My manager' placeholder.
features.on: No outbound email steps.

features.name: Rulesets
features.what: One per flow; a library default for new flows; edits apply immediately to all flows using it. Categories: flow properties (exclusivity, cool-off), outbound email (opt-out footer, can be locked on), response handling per event (reply, meeting, OOO, bounce → pause / remove / continue / remove whole account from all flows), flow end CRM status per end reason, CRM-change removal, flow status → CRM field (Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics).

features.on: No rulesets.

features.name: Ruleset beats outcome automation

features.gn: Quote: 'If the same outcome is configured in both a ruleset and an automation, the ruleset runs instead.'
features.on: No call-outcome automations. Outcomes (sold/go_back/…) only feed KPIs.

features.name: Company, personal and shared flows
features.what: Separate permissions to create company flows, create personal flows, and share personal flows.
features.gn: Separate permissions: create and manage company flows, create and manage personal flows, share personal flows. Engage analytics has a Flow visibility filter.
features.on: No flows.

features.name: Flows via API
features.what: List flows and folders; assign prospects; list flows per prospect; unassign by instance or CRM id.

features.name: AI flow builder

features.name: Migration from Outreach and Salesloft

modules.name: Dialer & call outcomes
modules.summary: The Gong dialer claims check out in detail (Twilio, seats, 36,000 min, local presence, trusted calling, per-region recording). We have no dialer at all, so phone capture depends on the browser extension. Our door-knock outcomes are the real analogue: a fixed 5-value enum, required on every knock, with an append-only undo. Sales-session outcomes, by contrast, are optional and in practice empty.

features.name: Click-to-call dialer

features.name: Default call outcomes
features.what: No answer: No voicemail, Left voicemail, Not in service, Busy. Answered: Follow up, Meeting booked, Bad timing, Has a solution, Bad persona, Wrong number, Gave referral, Bad fit, Opt out, Hung up, Gatekeeper, Not interested (other). Company-wide, one set.

features.name: Email tracking, branded links, opt-out

features.name: To-dos: recommended, flow, one-off

modules.name: Commercial model
modules.summary: Gong sells per-user licences plus a mandatory platform fee, modular since March 2025, with third-party reports of about $1,300-1,600 per user per year and metered AI credits on top. We are pilot-stage and not collecting money: plan tiers and billing fields exist in the vendor CRM, pilot codes provision access, and a $99-per-user pricing deck sits in docs.
modules.vsum: Pricing page, plans page and a third-party report (revenuegrid, cross-checked by WebSearch) confirm the claims; third-party figures vary, with some sources up to $1,920/user/yr.

features.name: Per-user licence plus platform fee
features.what: Licences are priced per user; a separate platform fee scales with users supported; integrations are free; quotes by form with team bands 1–50, 51–1,000, 1,001–9,999, 10,000+.
features.gn: 'Licenses are priced per user', 'platform fee based on the number of users supported', integrations free, team bands 1-50, 51-1,000, 1,001-9,999, 10,000+.
features.on: Per-user pricing is proposed ($99/user deck) and CRM has plan tiers (pilot/team_small/medium/large/enterprise), but billing_status defaults to not_collecting and Stripe isn't wired.

features.name: Modular since March 2025
features.what: Gong Foundation core plus Enable Essentials, Forecast Essentials, Gong Forecast, Gong Engage, Data Cloud; legacy bundles not renewed since March 2025.
features.gn: Foundation core plus Enable Essentials, Forecast Essentials, Gong Forecast, Engage, Data Cloud since March 2025; legacy plans move on renewal.
features.on: Modules exist (ELOSTATE, C.A.R.E, Sales Coach) and pilot codes provision per module, but no hard module gate; only the C.A.R.E extension is plan-gated.

features.name: Reported prices
features.what: Third-party procurement reports put Foundation at roughly $1,300–1,600 per user per year, a platform fee of $5,000–50,000 per year, and onboarding from about $7,500. Not confirmed by Gong.
features.gn: revenuegrid: $1,300-1,600/user/yr, platform fee $5k-50k, implementation $7,500-65,000; WebSearch shows other estimates up to $1,920 and onboarding up to $65k.
features.on: Our proposed price ($99/user, presumably monthly) is far below Gong's estimated per-seat cost; no platform or onboarding fee in code.

features.name: Metered AI credits

features.gn: 2,000 credits per paid core seat per year with purchasable extras confirmed.
